title: Documents silently unfindable via `_geoPolygon` after index build: cellulite leaves dead cell regions (~1% of clustered points)
body:
**Describe the bug**

After bulk-indexing ~50,000 documents whose `_geojson` Points are clustered in a small area, about 1.2% of them are **silently unfindable via `_geoPolygon`**, although:

- the documents are stored correctly (`GET /indexes/{index}/documents/{id}` shows the exact `_geojson`),
- the same documents **are** found via `_geoBoundingBox` over `_geo` with the same rectangle,
- all indexing tasks succeeded — nothing in task/batch details hints at the loss.

The loss is deterministic in the data and insertion order: the same documents disappear whether the corpus is sent as a single 50k payload, 5×10k, or 50×1k individually-awaited tasks, and the same document set is lost on v1.51.0, v1.52.0, and the current nightly.

The failure appears to be **positional (dead cell regions), not per-document**:

- re-sending the identical `_geojson`, nudging it by 1e-9°, or deleting and re-adding the document does not make it findable;
- a brand-new document inserted at an affected position is unfindable too;
- moving an affected document ≥0.1° away **into another populated region** and then back to its true position makes it findable at its true position (parking it in an empty far-away area does not);
- that park-and-restore recovers 100% of affected documents even in bulk (tested up to all 608 in one update task each way).

On our production index (31.5M documents, Germany-clustered), ~686k documents (~2.2%) are affected after a `filterableAttributes` reindex. A possibly related detail from its batch `progressTrace`: a single-document update spends >4 minutes in `indexing > writing geo points` and ~25s in `building geo json > remove deleted items from cells database` at this index size.

**To Reproduce**

Self-contained script (needs `curl`, `jq`, `python3`; against a fresh dev-mode instance):

1. `docker run -d --rm --name meili-geojson-repro -p 7700:7700 getmeili/meilisearch:v1.52`
2. Run `repro.sh` below. It seeds 50,000 deterministic pseudo-random points (seed 42) clustered in a 0.6°×0.6° box, each position stored in both `_geo` and `_geojson` (Point), both filterable.
3. Compare `_geoBoundingBox` (reads `_geo`) and `_geoPolygon` (reads `_geojson`) counts over the same rectangle, then watch the per-document recovery experiments.

<details>
<summary>repro.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Repro: documents silently missing from _geoPolygon (_geojson) after index build.
# Usage: MEILI_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7700 ./repro.sh
set -euo pipefail

URL="${MEILI_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:7700}"
IDX="geojson_repro"
POLY='_geoPolygon([50.9, 6.9], [50.9, 7.7], [51.7, 7.7], [51.7, 6.9])'
BBOX='_geoBoundingBox([51.7, 7.7], [50.9, 6.9])'
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

req() { curl -s -X "$1" "$URL$2" -H 'content-type: application/json' ${3:+-d "$3"}; }

wait_task() {
  local uid="$1" s
  while :; do
    s=$(curl -s "$URL/tasks/$uid" | jq -r .status)
    case "$s" in
      succeeded) return 0 ;;
      failed|canceled) echo "task $uid $s:" >&2; curl -s "$URL/tasks/$uid" | jq -c '.error' >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    sleep 0.2
  done
}

count() {
  req POST "/indexes/$IDX/search" \
    "$(jq -cn --arg f "$1" '{q:"",filter:$f,hitsPerPage:1,page:1}')" | jq -r .totalHits
}

echo "Meilisearch $(req GET /version | jq -r .pkgVersion)"

req DELETE "/indexes/$IDX" >/dev/null; sleep 1
wait_task "$(req POST /indexes "{\"uid\":\"$IDX\",\"primaryKey\":\"id\"}" | jq -r .taskUid)"
wait_task "$(req PATCH "/indexes/$IDX/settings" \
  '{"filterableAttributes":["_geo","_geojson","id"],"pagination":{"maxTotalHits":200000}}' | jq -r .taskUid)"

# 50,000 pseudo-random points clustered in a ~0.6 x 0.6 degree box (deterministic, seed 42),
# each carrying the same position as both _geo and a GeoJSON Point in _geojson.
python3 - "$WORK/seed.json" <<'PY'
import json, random, sys
random.seed(42)
docs = []
for i in range(50_000):
    lat = round(random.uniform(51.0, 51.6), 6)
    lng = round(random.uniform(7.0, 7.6), 6)
    docs.append({"id": f"s{i}", "_geo": {"lat": lat, "lng": lng},
                 "_geojson": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [lng, lat]}})
json.dump(docs, open(sys.argv[1], "w"))
PY

wait_task "$(curl -s -X POST "$URL/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary "@$WORK/seed.json" | jq -r .taskUid)"

echo "bbox matches via _geo:        $(count "$BBOX") / 50000"
echo "polygon matches via _geojson: $(count "$POLY") / 50000"

# Collect the ids the polygon filter CAN see, diff against all seeded ids.
page=1
while :; do
  hits=$(req POST "/indexes/$IDX/search" "$(jq -cn --arg f "$POLY" --argjson p "$page" \
    '{q:"",filter:$f,hitsPerPage:1000,page:$p,attributesToRetrieve:["id"]}')" | jq -r '.hits[].id')
  [[ -z "$hits" ]] && break
  echo "$hits" >> "$WORK/matched.txt"
  page=$((page + 1))
done
seq 0 49999 | sed 's/^/s/' | sort > "$WORK/all.txt"
sort "$WORK/matched.txt" | comm -23 "$WORK/all.txt" - > "$WORK/missing.txt"
echo "missing from polygon index:   $(wc -l < "$WORK/missing.txt") docs, e.g.:"
head -3 "$WORK/missing.txt"

lost=$(head -1 "$WORK/missing.txt")
doc=$(req GET "/indexes/$IDX/documents/$lost")
echo "stored doc $lost: $doc"
lat=$(jq -r ._geo.lat <<<"$doc"); lng=$(jq -r ._geo.lng <<<"$doc")

in_poly() { count "id = \"$lost\" AND $POLY"; }
echo "in polygon:                          $(in_poly)"

# (a) Update with the IDENTICAL _geojson value -> no recovery
wait_task "$(req PUT "/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  "[{\"id\":\"$lost\",\"_geojson\":{\"type\":\"Point\",\"coordinates\":[$lng,$lat]}}]" | jq -r .taskUid)"
echo "(a) after re-sending identical _geojson:      $(in_poly)"

# (b) Tiny nudge (lng + 1e-9, stays inside the same cell) -> still no recovery
wait_task "$(req PUT "/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  "[{\"id\":\"$lost\",\"_geojson\":{\"type\":\"Point\",\"coordinates\":[$(python3 -c "print($lng + 1e-9)"),$lat]}}]" | jq -r .taskUid)"
echo "(b) after tiny nudge (lng+1e-9):              $(in_poly)"

# (c) Fresh document at the same position -> also unfindable (the REGION is dead, not the doc)
wait_task "$(req POST "/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  "[{\"id\":\"fresh_at_dead_pos\",\"_geo\":{\"lat\":$lat,\"lng\":$lng},\"_geojson\":{\"type\":\"Point\",\"coordinates\":[$lng,$lat]}}]" | jq -r .taskUid)"
echo "(c) fresh doc at the same position:           $(count "id = \"fresh_at_dead_pos\" AND $POLY")"

# (d) Move the doc to an ALIVE spot inside the cluster, then back to its true position -> recovers
wait_task "$(req PUT "/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  "[{\"id\":\"$lost\",\"_geojson\":{\"type\":\"Point\",\"coordinates\":[7.312,51.312]}}]" | jq -r .taskUid)"
wait_task "$(req PUT "/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  "[{\"id\":\"$lost\",\"_geojson\":{\"type\":\"Point\",\"coordinates\":[$lng,$lat]}}]" | jq -r .taskUid)"
echo "(d) after park at alive spot + restore:       $(in_poly)"

# (e) Same round-trip but parked FAR OUTSIDE the seeded cluster -> does NOT recover
next=$(sed -n 2p "$WORK/missing.txt")
ndoc=$(req GET "/indexes/$IDX/documents/$next")
nlat=$(jq -r ._geo.lat <<<"$ndoc"); nlng=$(jq -r ._geo.lng <<<"$ndoc")
wait_task "$(req PUT "/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  "[{\"id\":\"$next\",\"_geojson\":{\"type\":\"Point\",\"coordinates\":[40.0,10.0]}}]" | jq -r .taskUid)"
wait_task "$(req PUT "/indexes/$IDX/documents" \
  "[{\"id\":\"$next\",\"_geojson\":{\"type\":\"Point\",\"coordinates\":[$nlng,$nlat]}}]" | jq -r .taskUid)"
echo "(e) same, but parked far outside the cluster: $(count "id = \"$next\" AND $POLY")"
```

</details>

**Expected behavior**

Every document with a valid `_geojson` Point inside the polygon is returned by `_geoPolygon`; counts match `_geoBoundingBox` over the same rectangle (modulo boundary inclusivity).

**Screenshots**

Not applicable — full terminal output of the script (v1.52.0; nightly output is identical, including the same lost-document ids):

```
Meilisearch 1.52.0
bbox matches via _geo:        50000 / 50000
polygon matches via _geojson: 49392 / 50000
missing from polygon index:   608 docs, e.g.:
s10005
s10036
s10054
stored doc s10005: {"id":"s10005","_geo":{"lat":51.088298,"lng":7.108557},"_geojson":{"type":"Point","coordinates":[7.108557,51.088298]}}
in polygon:                          0
(a) after re-sending identical _geojson:      0
(b) after tiny nudge (lng+1e-9):              0
(c) fresh doc at the same position:           0
(d) after park at alive spot + restore:       1
(e) same, but parked far outside the cluster: 0
```

**Meilisearch version:**

v1.51.0, v1.52.0, and nightly (commit `271141f8ff19bd6685b2b82afc08dc873197113d`, image built 2026-08-05) — identical behavior, including identical lost-document sets.

**Additional context**

- Official Docker images, Linux x86_64, default configuration, no master key. Index settings: `filterableAttributes: ["_geo", "_geojson", "id"]`, 50,000 documents.
- The symptom is the `_geojson` twin of #5331 (`_geo` entries lost on document update, fixed in v1.13), but here the loss happens at initial build/reindex time and affects positions, not documents.
- The recovery matrix above (identical rewrite ✗ / tiny nudge ✗ / fresh doc at position ✗ / round-trip via populated region ✓ / round-trip via empty region ✗) hopefully narrows the search: it looks like items present when a cell splits can end up associated with a cell the query side never visits, and only a transit through another populated cell re-registers them.
- AI disclosure: this bug was investigated and this report drafted with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5 orchestrating Opus 5 subagents), supervised by a human engineer. The reproduction script and all numbers above were re-run and verified against fresh containers before filing.
- If it helps, I'd be happy to try contributing a fix PR in the next weeks — with the caveat that I'm not a Rust developer, so it would be an AI-authored fix under my supervision. Happy to leave it to the team instead if you'd rather not review that.

title: download-latest.sh: detect and reject musl-based Linux distributions
body:
## Related issue
Fixes #4379

## Summary
`download-latest.sh` didn't detect musl-based Linux distributions (e.g. Alpine), so it would download a glibc binary that fails to run there. This adds an `is_musl` check (via `ldd --version`, since musl's `ldd` prints "musl libc" on its first line, unlike glibc's "ldd (GNU libc) ...") called from `fill_release_variables()` right after the OS is determined, exiting early with a clear `musl_failure_usage` message instead.

Three earlier attempts at this issue (#6487, #6242, #4386) were closed. Looking at #6487 specifically, the review feedback was that its detection functions were defined but never actually called anywhere in the script. This PR wires the check into the actual control flow.

## Manual verification
- Ran the real, modified script on this (glibc) machine — completes normally, downloads and runs as before.
- Mocked `ldd --version` to output `musl libc ...` and re-ran the real script end-to-end: exits 1 with the `musl_failure_usage` message, no download attempted.
- `sh -n download-latest.sh` — syntax check passes.

title: Repeated crashes due to SIGSEGV in mimalloc during concurrent federated search formatting and indexing (v1.51, Linux AArch64)
body:
**Describe the bug**
We’ve had Meilisearch crash at least three times in production after upgrading from a v1.3x release to v1.51.0.

Each time, systemd reports a native segfault:
```
Main process exited, code=dumped, status=11/SEGV
```

The core dumps point to the same general path: mimalloc while Meilisearch is formatting results for a federated search.

```
mi_heap_malloc_zero_aligned_at_generic
MatchesIter::next
Matcher::compute_matches
Matcher::format
format_fields
HitMaker::make_hit
SearchByIndex::execute
```

Other threads were indexing documents and writing to LMDB at the same time.
This doesn’t appear to be an OOM issue. The server has 64 GiB of RAM, little swap usage, and no corresponding kernel OOM event.

**To Reproduce**
We don’t have a reliable standalone reproduction yet. It happens under normal production traffic with indexing and federated searches running concurrently. Indexing is limited to two threads and 12 GiB of memory.

**Expected behavior**
Concurrent indexing and searching should not terminate the Meilisearch process.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Meilisearch version:**
v1.51.0, upgraded from a v1.3x release.

title: Fix code security issues in GitHub Actions workflows
body:
## What this PR does

Fixes 53 high-severity SAST findings (Bastion security scan) in the CI/CD configuration:

### Pin all mutable action tags to full commit SHAs (49 findings, 16 workflow files)
Every `uses: action@tag` reference is now pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA with a trailing version comment (e.g. `actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6`). Tags and branches can be silently repointed by the action owner, enabling supply-chain attacks (as seen in the trivy-action and tj-actions compromises).

`dtolnay/rust-toolchain` also gets an explicit `toolchain:` input, since it normally infers the toolchain from the ref name — which is no longer possible when pinned to a SHA.

Dependabot already covers `github-actions` monthly, so pinned SHAs will keep being bumped automatically.

### Scope `MEILI_BOT_GH_PAT` to the steps that need it (2 findings)
In `update-cargo-toml-version.yml` and `bench-pr.yml`, `GH_TOKEN` was declared in the workflow-level `env:` block, exposing it to every step. It is now referenced only by the steps that actually use it.

### Remove dead `curl | sh` install path (1 finding)
The Go SDK test job still had the legacy `golang/dep` install (`curl … | sh`) behind `if [ -f Gopkg.toml ]`. meilisearch-go uses Go modules, so this branch never executed — removed.

### Add Dependabot cooldown (1 finding)
`cooldown: default-days: 7` on the `github-actions` ecosystem, so newly published action versions wait 7 days before update PRs (protects against compromised releases being pulled in immediately).

All 53 findings have been closed in Bastion with a reference to this change.

title: Expose per-index `databaseSize` and `usedDatabaseSize` in the stats routes
body:
### Motivation

Compaction is per index. `POST /indexes/{index_uid}/compact` reclaims free pages for a single index.

The stats routes do not match that granularity. `GET /stats` reports `databaseSize` and `usedDatabaseSize` for the whole instance only, so there is no way to answer the question that decides whether to compact: *which index is holding the reclaimable space?*

Today the operator has to compact indexes one by one and diff the global figure after each run, which is expensive on large databases. On Cloud this is the main blocker for building any automated or advisory compaction workflow, since we cannot rank indexes by reclaimable space.

### Current behaviour

In `create_all_stats` (`crates/meilisearch/src/routes/mod.rs`) the per-index sizes are read and accumulated into the global total, then discarded:

```rust
let stats = index_scheduler.user_index_stats(&index_uid)?;
database_size += stats.inner_stats.database_size;
used_database_size += stats.inner_stats.used_database_size;
```

And in `IndexStats::from_db_index_stats` (`crates/meilisearch/src/routes/indexes/mod.rs`) they are explicitly destructured away:

```rust
database_size: _,
used_database_size: _,
```

The values themselves already exist on `index_scheduler::IndexStats`, computed by `IndexStats::new` from `index.on_disk_size()` and `index.used_size()`, and cached in the `index-stats` database. Exposing them adds no computation and does not require opening the index.

### Proposed API

Additive only. Two new fields on `IndexStats`, returned unconditionally, formatted through the existing `Size` type so they honour `sizeFormat=raw|human`.

**`GET /indexes/{index_uid}/stats`**

```json
{
  "numberOfDocuments": 10,
  "databaseSize": 1572864,
  "usedDatabaseSize": 524288,
  "rawDocumentDbSize": 100,
  "avgDocumentSize": 10,
  "isIndexing": false,
  "fieldDistribution": { "genre": 10, "author": 9 }
}
```

**`GET /stats`**

```json
{
  "databaseSize": 2621440,
  "usedDatabaseSize": 1048576,
  "lastUpdate": "2019-11-20T09:40:33.711324Z",
  "indexes": {
    "movies": {
      "numberOfDocuments": 10,
      "databaseSize": 1572864,
      "usedDatabaseSize": 524288,
      "rawDocumentDbSize": 100,
      "avgDocumentSize": 10,
      "isIndexing": false,
      "fieldDistribution": { "genre": 10, "author": 9 }
    },
    "products": {
      "numberOfDocuments": 4,
      "databaseSize": 786432,
      "usedDatabaseSize": 262144,
      "rawDocumentDbSize": 40,
      "avgDocumentSize": 10,
      "isIndexing": false,
      "fieldDistribution": { "sku": 4 }
    }
  }
}
```

Field semantics, matching the existing doc comments on `index_scheduler::IndexStats`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `databaseSize` | On-disk size of the index LMDB environment, used and free pages included |
| `usedDatabaseSize` | Size of the used pages only |

The difference between the two is the reclaimable space, which is what compaction targets. Clients can derive it, so no third field is needed.

The fields are returned unconditionally rather than behind a query parameter, since they are the same class of information as the existing global `databaseSize`, unlike the verbose `internalDatabaseSizes`.

### Considerations

- Purely additive, no breaking change. Existing clients ignore the new keys.
- No performance cost: values come from the cached `index-stats` entry, so no index open and no extra LMDB read beyond what the route already does.
- Documentation for `GET /stats` and `GET /indexes/{index_uid}/stats` needs the two new fields, plus a note that per-index sizes are not expected to sum exactly to the instance total.

title: Duplicate pinned documents in federated search
body:
**Describe the bug**
Pinned documents are not correctly deduplicated in federated search requests containing several queries hitting the same index.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Enable the dsr experimental feature
2. Add a rule with an action to pin a document
3. Create a federated search request containing 2 queries that target the same index and firing the DSR
4. Observe the document being pinned twice.

**Expected behavior**
The document is only pinned once.

**Meilisearch version:**
The work on DSR as index did not modify the way pins are resolved, so this likely dates back from the original introduction of pinning in v1.41

title: search rejects facets ["*"] with invalid_search_facets on filterable attributes
body:
**Describe the bug**
`POST /indexes/:uid/search` rejects `facets: ["*"]` with `invalid_search_facets`, even when the index has valid `filterableAttributes`.

Observed error:
`Invalid facet distribution: Pattern '*' is not filterable. Available filterable attributes patterns are: 'tag'.`
Also reproduced with `'year'`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run `getmeili/meilisearch-enterprise:nightly`
2. Create an index, add documents containing a field like `tag` or `year`
3. Set `filterableAttributes` to `["tag"]` or `["year"]`
4. Call `POST /indexes/:uid/search` with body:
   ```json
   {
     "q": "prince",
     "facets": ["*"]
   }
   ```
5. See `400 invalid_search_facets`

Minimal repro also works with an empty query:
```json
{
  "q": "",
  "facets": ["*"]
}
```

**Expected behavior**
`facets: ["*"]` should return facet distribution / facet stats for all filterable attributes, not fail validation.

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Meilisearch version:**
`getmeili/meilisearch-enterprise:nightly` Observed in the scheduled [SDK CI run on 2026-07-21](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/actions/runs/29808755246)

**Additional context**
- Confirmed in SDK CI failures for:
  - Dart
  - Go
  - Rust
- Example failing requests:
  - `filterableAttributes = ["tag"]` + `facets = ["*"]`
  - `filterableAttributes = ["year"]` + `facets = ["*"]`
- This looks like a regression in wildcard facet validation: `"*"` appears to be validated like a literal pattern instead of preserving its old meaning: "all filterable facets".

title: Prune cancelled waiters from the search queue
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #6508

## Changelog

Fix a bug where a search request that was cancelled while waiting for a search-queue permit could leave a stale entry in the internal search queue. The cancelled request kept occupying a capacity slot, which could cause a live request to be wrongly rejected with `TooManySearchRequests`, waste a scheduling turn delivering a permit to a gone request, and inflate the `searches_waiting` metric.

## Implementation

`SearchQueue::run` stores each waiter's `oneshot::Sender<Permit>` in a `Vec` and uses `queue.len()` to drive capacity enforcement, random eviction, permit selection, and the `searches_waiting` metric. When a request future is cancelled after its sender has been handed to the scheduler but before a permit is delivered, only the receiver is dropped — the scheduler keeps the now-closed sender, so the stale entry keeps participating in all of those decisions.

The scheduler now calls `queue.retain(|waiter| !waiter.is_closed())` at the start of both `tokio::select!` arms:

- before delivering a freed permit (so a live waiter, not a cancelled one, receives it and cancelled waiters are not counted), and
- before the capacity / eviction checks for an incoming request (so a cancelled waiter can neither occupy a capacity slot nor evict a live waiter).

`oneshot::Sender::is_closed()` is exactly the "the receiver was dropped / the request was cancelled" signal, so after pruning `queue.len()` reflects only live waiters.

The change is confined to the scheduler loop; there is no change to the public API, to `Permit`, or to `try_get_search_permit`.

### Test

Added a deterministic regression test `cancelled_waiter_is_pruned_from_search_queue` in `crates/meilisearch/src/search_queue.rs`. It holds the single running permit for the whole test (so no `search_finished` event fires and no random permit selection happens) and uses a capacity large enough that no eviction ever happens, exercising only the new-request pruning path. It cancels one waiter and asserts the queue converges to exactly the live waiters. The test fails against the previous behavior (the cancelled waiter is still counted) and passes with the fix. It uses a bounded yield-loop rather than sleeps, so it is not timing-flaky.

Run it with:

```bash
cargo test -p meilisearch --lib search_queue::tests::cancelled_waiter_is_pruned_from_search_queue
```

title: String sorting does not follow the Ukrainian alphabet order for `ґ` and `і`
body:
Hi)

When sorting a string attribute containing Ukrainian words, the results do not follow the Ukrainian alphabetical order.

In particular, words containing the Ukrainian letters `ґ` and `і` are placed incorrectly.

The returned order appears to be based on Unicode code points rather than Ukrainian locale-aware collation rules.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create an index and add `name` to the `sortableAttributes` setting.
2. Add the following documents:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "ікло"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "name": "яблуко"
  },
  {
    "id": 3,
    "name": "ананас"
  },
  {
    "id": 4,
    "name": "ґрати"
  },
  {
    "id": 5,
    "name": "banana"
  }
]
3. Perform a search using descending sorting:
{
  "q": "",
  ...
  "sort": ["name:desc"]
}

Actual behavior:

The documents are returned in the following order:

ґрати
ікло
яблуко
ананас
banana

Expected behavior:

According to the Ukrainian alphabet, the Ukrainian words should be sorted in descending order as follows:

яблуко
ікло
ґрати
ананас
banana

The Ukrainian alphabet places ґ after г, while і comes after и. Therefore, the current result does not correspond to Ukrainian alphabetical order.

The position of Latin-script values such as banana may depend on the selected collation rules, but the relative order of Ukrainian words should follow the Ukrainian alphabet.

Meilisearch version: 1.45.0, Docker-image


Thank you in advance)

title: docs-site: Sourcey-generated static docs (Frantic bounty #46)
body:
## What

This PR adds a `docs-site/` directory containing a complete **Sourcey 3.6.5** static docs build for Meilisearch.

- **OpenAPI spec**: `meilisearch-openapi.json` from the v1.49.0 release (pinned to upstream commit `17758dce3fcc21d8e2415176c29d1106e905de00`)
- **Spec format**: OpenAPI 3.1.0, 69 paths, 139 operations, MIT licensed
- **Generator**: `sourcey@3.6.5` (openapi + markdown adapters)
- **Output**: 5-page static HTML site with full navigation, search index (347 entries), and llms.txt / llms-full.txt exports

## Why

Frantic bounty #46 — "Publish Sourcey docs for a second ecosystem" ($16) — requires Sourcey to prove it can handle more than one language ecosystem. The live Frantic board already has Go (godoc) and C++ (Doxygen) first-ecosystem proofs; this PR adds **Rust** as a second ecosystem by using Meilisearch's official OpenAPI spec as the target.

## Adoption path

If Meilisearch maintainers want to adopt this, the natural next step is to enable GitHub Pages from the `docs-site/dist/` tree on this branch (or merge this PR with a `.github/workflows/pages.yml` workflow that builds and deploys it). The `docs-site/README.md` has the full build instructions for maintainers.

## Why this is a "credible durable home the project owns"

The bounty acceptance criteria disqualify personal hosts (`<handle>.github.io`, Vercel subdomains, demo orgs, raw.githack, etc.). This PR puts the docs **inside the project repository** at a known commit, which is the most direct possible interpretation of "the target project's real site/repo."

## Tested

`sourcey build` produces 5 pages (introduction, quickstart, concepts, adapter-notes, api) and a 347-entry search index. Total artifact size ~12 MB. All files are pinned to the v1.49.0 release tag.

## Notes

- I'm submitting this as part of a Frantic paid-workflow. The repo is a public fork (`jdjioe5-cpu/jdjioe5-cpu-meilisearch`); the PR is opened directly against `meilisearch/meilisearch` for maintainer review.
- The `docs-site/dist/` contents are the actual rendered output; reviewers can `python3 -m http.server` from `docs-site/dist/` to view the rendered site locally.

title: Add filter condition to DSRs
body:
## Changelog

### New `filter` rule activation condition

Dynamic search rules (DSR) can now declare a new `filter` condition: it contains a single `values` key, whose value is a JSON object.
The keys of this `values` JSON object are the  facet names (e.g.  `color`, `genres`, ...), while their values are the values that a filter must resolve to for these facets, so that the rule is active.

<details>

<summary>Example of sending a DSR with a filter condition</summary>


```jsonc
// PATCH /dynamic-search-rules/test-filter

{
  "conditions": {
    "filter": {
      "values": {
        "color": "red",
        "category": "shirt"
      }
    }
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "selector": { "id": "red shirt on sales" },
      "action": { "type": "pin", "position": 0 }
    }
  ]
}
```


</details>

<details>
<summary>Example of search query that enables the DSR above</summary>

```jsonc
{
  "filter": "(category = shirt AND color = red) OR (category = jeans AND color = blue)"
}
```

</details>

Note that the filter only needs to have one branch resolving to all the facet values declared in the rule for the rule to be active.

### New `lastUpdatedAt` field

Dynamic search rules returned by `GET /dynamic-search-rules/{:ruleUid}` and `POST /dynamic-search-rules` contain an additional `lastUpdatedAt` field. 

This field is automatically updated with the `enqueuedAt` value of the last task that modified the rule.

### Rules are listed with the most recently updated first

`POST /dynamic-search-rules` now lists rules in descending `lastUpdatedAt` order, meaning that the most recently updated rules will be listed first.

### New environment variables

New environment variables are defined to control the behavior of the DSR fuel:

- `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_FILTER_FUEL` (in range 0..4294967296): controls how many filter constraint combinations Meilisearch will attempt to resolve at search time before giving up and applying partial rules.
- `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_FILTER_OR_FUEL` (in range 0..65536): controls how many filter disjunctions Meilisearch will build when turning a filter to its canonical shape
- `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_FILTER_AND_FUEL` (in range 0..65536): controls how many filter conjunctions Meilisearch will build in total when turning a filter to its canonical shape
- `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_FILTER_DEPTH_FUEL` (in range 0..256): controls the maximum recursive depth that Meilisearch allows when turning a filter to its canonical shape

## Implementation

- Modify the way updates to DSR are handled: updated rules are now computed by merging the previous and new versions of the rule, and the computed payload is now a replacement rather than an update.
- Add DSR index upgrade logic that reapplies the dsr settings if in a given version range.

body:
# Changelog

Adds a new route `GET /indexes/{:indexId}/settings/target`

Calling this route returns an object with the following fields:

- `current`: settings object representing the currently processed state of the settings. `null` if the index does not currently exist
- `target`: settings object representing the target processing state of the settings, as obtained by processing all related tasks. `null` if the index will be deleted after processing all related tasks.
- `taskIds`: list of task IDs that will modify the setting of the index or delete the index.
- `needsProcessing`: set to `true` if there is at least one task that will update the settings of this index.

Returns 404 `index_not_found` if called on an index that doesn't currently exist **and** no tasks related to this index are pending (enqueued or processing).

title: Support attribute patterns when asking for facet distribution
body:
## Changelog

The `facets` parameter in search and federated search now supports more wildcards. Previously, only the single wildcard `"*"` was supported, requesting all filterable fields.

Now, patterns *containing* `*`  are supported with the same matching rules as in `filterableAttributes.attributePatterns` and `localizedAttributes.attributePatterns`, such as `dogs.*`, which will add to the facet distribution all filterable fields that match the pattern (such as `dogs.intel`, `dogs.kefir`, etc.).

---


This PR enables providing patterns when requesting the facet distribution of certain fields. Before, it was only possible to provide either a whole attribute name, i.e., `title`, `dogs.intel`, or everything through the `*` special pattern. Now, a user can provide patterns, i.e., `title`, `dogs.*`, `*` and retrieve all of the facets that are filterable. An error is still thrown if a pattern is found to match a non-filterable pattern or matches nothing in the filterable attributes list.

title: Respect pagination.maxTotalHits in total hits metadata
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #6482

## What happens

With `pagination.maxTotalHits` set, the returned `hits` were correctly capped, but the response metadata was not:

- page-based pagination reported uncapped `totalHits` / `totalPages`
- offset/limit pagination reported an uncapped `estimatedTotalHits`

This is a regression: single-index searches now go through the federated search path (`perform_federated_search`), which built the estimated total straight from the candidate count. The setting was read and applied to `required_hit_count` (so `hits` stayed capped) but not to `estimated_total_hits`. The non-federated `perform_search` path still capped it with `min(candidates.len(), max_total_hits)`, hence the divergence.

## Fix

Cap the estimated total by `maxTotalHits` in the federated path, matching the non-federated path and the documented behavior that both `totalHits` and `totalPages` are computed only until they reach `pagination.maxTotalHits`.

Reproduced with 3 documents and `maxTotalHits = 2`: before the fix `totalHits`/`totalPages`/`estimatedTotalHits` were `3`; after, they are `2`, while `hits` are unchanged.

# summary

Support sharding and network on **GET** `indexes/:uid/documents`, **GET** `indexes/:uid/documents/:document_id` and on **POST** `indexes/:uid/documents/fetch`

# Changelog

**GET** `indexes/:uid/documents`, **GET** `indexes/:uid/documents/:document_id` and **POST** `indexes/:uid/documents/fetch` will now fetch the documents from all the shards in the configured network.

Moreover, a new `useNetwork` parameter is available to activate or deactivate the usage of the network.

## Breaking change

The default behavior for users using the network experimental feature will change on the following routes:
- **GET** `indexes/:uid/documents`
- **GET** `indexes/:uid/documents/:document_id`
- **POST** `indexes/:uid/documents/fetch`

Meilisearch will now fetch the documents from all the shards and not only on the local machine when processing the request.
To keep the same behavior as before, users will have to set `useNetwork` to `false` when making their request.

title: Escaped quotes/backslashes in filters return `invalid_search_filter` error
body:
## Describe the bug
A filter expression containing escaped backslashes and double quotes in both the attribute name and value is rejected by Meilisearch with `invalid_search_filter`. 

## Expected behavior
The request should be accepted and parsed as a valid filter, as it was in earlier versions. The server should not reject properly escaped quoted attribute/value pairs.

## Actual behavior
Meilisearch returns HTTP `400` with `invalid_search_filter`, e.g. `Was expecting an operation ... at "\"crazy_\\_\\\"field\\\"\" = \"real \\\\\"crazy\\\"\""`. The same payload previously worked.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create an index, make the unusual field filterable, and add one document:
```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer masterKey' \
  --data-binary '{"uid":"movies","primaryKey":"id"}'

curl -X PATCH 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/movies/settings/filterable-attributes' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer masterKey' \
  --data-binary '["crazy_\\_\"field\""]'

curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/movies/documents' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer masterKey' \
  --data-binary '[{"id":1,"crazy_\\_\"field\"":"real \\\"crazy\\\""}]'
```

2. Run a `multi-search` using the escaped filter:
```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/multi-search' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer masterKey' \
  --data-binary '{
    "queries": [
      {
        "indexUid": "movies",
        "q": "",
        "filter": ["\"crazy_\\\\_\\\\\\\"field\\\\\\\"\"=\"real \\\\\\\"crazy\\\\\\\"\""]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

3. Observe that the server returns `400 invalid_search_filter` instead of accepting the query.

## Version
Reproduced on `v1.48.3`

## Additional context (optional)
This bug is visible in `meilisearch-js-plugins` [failing SDK tests](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/actions/runs/28733007711/job/85202058112)

title: refactor(milli): unify exact and tolerant words in a single words FST
body: ## Summary Fixes #6440 This PR unifies exact-word and typo-tolerant word dictionaries into a single `words_fst`. It builds on the exact-word prefix search work from #6403 / #6432, simplifying the implementation by including exact words directly in the main FST instead of maintaining a separate registration path. ## What changed - **Unified FST Building**: - Exact words are now registered normally in `words_fst` using `register_word` instead of being handled separately. - Removed `register_exact_word_for_prefixes` from `WordFstBuilder` as prefixes for all words (tolerant + exact) are now generated naturally during the main FST build. - **Simplified Post-Processing**: - In `compute_word_fst`, combined `word_delta` and `exact_word_delta` into a single `WordDelta` to build a single unified FST. - In `recompute_word_fst_from_word_docids_database`, performed a sorted merge-join of `word_docids` and `exact_word_docids` to rebuild the unified FST. - In `recompute_exact_word_prefix_docids_from_database`, removed manual collection and registration of exact words, draining directly from the unified `words_fst`. - **Migration & Upgrade**: - Added a `RecomputeWordFstAndPrefixes` dumpless upgrade task in `v1_49.rs` (checking `initial_version < 1.49.0`) to automatically rebuild the words FST to include exact words and regenerate prefix databases for existing indexes on boot. ## Behavior Preserved - `word_docids` (typo-tolerant) and `exact_word_docids` (exact attributes/numbers) remain separate LMDB databases. - Typo derivations only query `word_docids`. Even though exact words now reside in the main FST, querying them for typo derivations yields 0 hits, preserving exact-attribute typo rules. - Prefix search on exact attributes (`exact_word_prefix_docids`) functions as expected. ## Test Plan - [x] Ran the full search test suite sequentially: ```bash cargo test --package milli --test mod -- --test-threads=1 ## Generative AI Disclosure - [x] I used generative AI tools to assist in researching, refactoring, and drafting code for this PR all code was manually reviewed, verified, and tested locally prior to submission.

title: Add musl detection in download-latest.sh
body:
Fixes #4379

Trying to install meilisearch on Alpine right now silently downloads a binary that then fails to start, because the prebuilt artifacts are glibc-linked. This PR makes `download-latest.sh` detect that case and exit with a clear error before touching the network.

The check is just `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` — it's empty on musl, populated on glibc. I also gate it on `os == linux` so non-Linux hosts keep their current behaviour.

Tested locally on macOS (no false positive) and with an empty `getconf` to simulate a musl host (correctly triggers the error). I didn't add a test because the repo doesn't have a test harness for shell scripts; if you want one I can add a small bats file, but figured the change is small enough that the script change is its own test.

Happy to adjust wording on the error message if you want a different tone.

title: DSR as index, mk II
body:
## Breaking changes

This PR introduces several breaking changes

### Request type changes

1. `priority` has been replaced with `precedence`, which better reflects the behavior (lower precedence means the rule is applied first)
2. `conditions` has been modified from an array to an object with two fields: "query" of type `QueryCondition` and "time" of time `TimeCondition`
3. New type `QueryCondition` that contains the fields `isEmpty` (as previously) and `words` instead of `contains` (same type)
4. It is now possible to pass `isEmpty: false` with `words` in a `QueryCondition`. Passing `isEmpty:true` with `words` still results in a synchronous error.
5. New type `TimeCondition` with fields `start` and `end` (unchanged semantics from previous type).
6. When specifying the `selector` of an `Action`, it is now mandatory to specify an `id`. Previously, it was optional, but the action would never trigger.
7. When listing rules with `POST /dynamic-search-rules`, `filter.attributePatterns` has been replaced with `filter.query`, an optional string that searches in rule `description` and `conditions.query.words`.
8. When calling `DELETE /dynamic-search-rules/{:ruleUid}` or `PATCH /dynamic-search-rules/{:ruleUid}` in a sharded configuration, endpoint will not return a HTTP 400 error if called on a follower remote rather than on the leader.

### Response changes

1. `PATCH /dynamic-search-rules/{:ruleUid}` and `DELETE /dynamic-search-rules/{:ruleUid}` now register an asynchronous task..
2. The response is modified to return the registered task instead of the modified dynamic search rule.
3. HTTP 404 is no longer returned if the `{:ruleUid}` portion of the URL refers to a rule that doesn't exist. This is because rules are processed asynchronously, and is consistent with the behavior of `DELETE /indexes/{:indexUid}/documents/{:docId}` for `{:docId}` 

## Behavior changes

- The `conditions.query.words` behaves differently from `query.contains`: previously, a rule would match if its conditions `query.contains` would be substrings of `q` in the search query in the sense of [`str::contains`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html#method.contains). Now, a rule matches if all the words in `conditions.query.words` appear in `q` (after normalization). For `q = hero super`, `query.contains = super hero` would **not** match, whereas `conditions.query.words = super hero` does now match. This behavior is more in line with regular search, and allows improving performance.
- Dynamic search rules are now replicated from the leader to its follower, when in a sharded configuration

## Additions

- Add a new `DELETE /dynamic-search-rule` route that deletes all the DSRs
- Add the concept of "DSR fuel" that determines how much energy is spent resolving DSR during a search. The fuel is initialized with some default variables that can be overriden using environment variables:
    - `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_MAX_COUNTED_WORDS`: max number of words considered inside of a search query for the purpose of finding `conditions.query.words` constraints. Defaults to 10, max value is 255
    - `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_MAX_ACTIVE_RULES`: max number of active rules whose actions are evaluated. Defaults to 1000, max value is 4294967295
    - `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_MAX_PIN_ACTIONS`: max number of pin actions that are applied. Defaults to 100, max value is 4294967295
    - `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DSR_FUEL_WORD_FUEL`: max number of constraint combinations that are evaluated for the purpose of finding `conditions.query.words` constraints. Defaults to 4096, max value is 4294967295

## Implementation changes

- Introduce a special dsr index. It is created if missing when creating a DSR
    - It is snapshotted and saved/restored in dumps 
    - It is migrated along with other indexes during dumpless upgrade
    - It is replicated during network rebalancing, from the leader's version of the index
- Introduce several `IndexUid` types, to represent validated user indexes or the special dsr index.
- Make index mapper implementation generic over the IndexUid type
- Add DSR related tasks
- Search changes:
    -  Build located query term before calling execute_search, resolve pins there
    -  Filtered universe optionally accepts a set of base candidates
    - Use time OffsetDateTime instead of std::Instant to measure elpased time
    - Pass uid and OffsetDateTime to lower levels in search so they can be used to resolve DSRs

title: Support target index names in the export route
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #6049

## What does this PR do?

Adds support for target index names in the export route, as described in the issue and agreed in the discussion.

A new optional `name` field is added to the per-index export settings:

- The `$name` variable in the value is replaced with the matched source index name, e.g. `"name": "mega-$name"` exports `super-toto` and `super-boby` to `mega-super-toto` and `mega-super-boby`.
- A value without the variable is used as-is (static name), e.g. `"name": "everyone"`.
- Omitting the field keeps the current behaviour of reusing the source index name.

```json
// POST /export
{
  "url": "http://ms-xxx-yy.fra.meilisearch.com",
  "indexes": {
    "super-*": { "name": "mega-$name", "filter": "super-power = laser" }
  }
}
```

The resolved name is validated as a valid index uid. As discussed, if several source indexes resolve to the **same** target name the task fails with a clear error listing the colliding indexes (since the processing order of indexes is not deterministic, erroring is preferable to a silent last-one-wins merge).

Implementation notes:
- `name` is threaded from the route payload (`routes/export.rs`) through the task type (`meilisearch-types/tasks`) to `process_export`.
- The resolution + collision logic is extracted into a small `resolve_target_index_names` helper, which is unit-tested directly (the export route itself talks to a remote instance and has no automated test harness in the repo).
- The field is added with `#[serde(default)]` so already-enqueued export tasks keep deserializing.

title: `totalHits` and `totalPages` ignore `pagination.maxTotalHits` with page-based pagination
body:
## Describe the bug

With page-based pagination (`page` + `hitsPerPage`) and `pagination.maxTotalHits = 2`, recent Meilisearch versions return uncapped `totalHits` / `totalPages` metadata even though the returned `hits` remain capped.

This looks like a regression from `v1.46.0` to `v1.48.3`.

## Expected behavior

`totalHits` and `totalPages` should respect `pagination.maxTotalHits` for page-based pagination.

With 3 indexed documents and `maxTotalHits = 2`:

- `totalHits` should be `2`
- with `hitsPerPage = 1`, `totalPages` should be `2`
- metadata should not indicate a third reachable hit/page when only the first 2 hits are exposed

This matches the Search API spec:

> Both `totalPages` and `totalHits` are computed until they reach the `pagination.maxTotalHits` number from the settings.

# Actual behavior

For the same dataset and queries:

- `hits` are identical between versions
- `v1.46.0` returns capped metadata
- `v1.48.3` returns uncapped metadata

Example for `{"q":"","page":1,"hitsPerPage":1}`:

```text
// v1.46.0
{"ids":[1],"hitsCount":1,"totalHits":2,"totalPages":2,"page":1,"hitsPerPage":1}

// v1.48.3
{"ids":[1],"hitsCount":1,"totalHits":3,"totalPages":3,"page":1,"hitsPerPage":1}
```

Example for `{"q":"","page":2,"hitsPerPage":1}`:

```text
// v1.46.0
{"ids":[2],"hitsCount":1,"totalHits":2,"totalPages":2,"page":2,"hitsPerPage":1}

// v1.48.3
{"ids":[2],"hitsCount":1,"totalHits":3,"totalPages":3,"page":2,"hitsPerPage":1}
```

## Steps to reproduce

Minimal raw HTTP repro using two Docker containers:

```bash
set -euo pipefail

OLD_PORT=17700
NEW_PORT=17701
KEY='masterKey'
OLD_NAME='ms-old-repro'
NEW_NAME='ms-new-repro'

docker run -d --rm --name "$OLD_NAME" -p ${OLD_PORT}:7700 -e MEILI_MASTER_KEY="$KEY" getmeili/meilisearch-enterprise:v1.46.0
docker run -d --rm --name "$NEW_NAME" -p ${NEW_PORT}:7700 -e MEILI_MASTER_KEY="$KEY" getmeili/meilisearch-enterprise:v1.48.3

cleanup() {
  docker stop "$OLD_NAME" "$NEW_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

wait_task() {
  local port="$1"
  local uid="$2"
  local task_status

  while true; do
    task_status=$(curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/tasks/${uid}" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" | jq -r '.status')
    case "$task_status" in
      succeeded) return 0 ;;
      failed|canceled)
        echo "Task ${uid} on port ${port} ended with status: ${task_status}" >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    sleep 0.2
  done
}

for p in $OLD_PORT $NEW_PORT; do
  until curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:${p}/health" >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done

  create_task_uid=$(curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${p}/indexes" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data '{"uid":"books","primaryKey":"id"}' | jq -r '.taskUid')
  wait_task "$p" "$create_task_uid"

  settings_task_uid=$(curl -sS -X PATCH "http://127.0.0.1:${p}/indexes/books/settings/pagination" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data '{"maxTotalHits":2}' | jq -r '.taskUid')
  wait_task "$p" "$settings_task_uid"

  documents_task_uid=$(curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${p}/indexes/books/documents" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data '[{"id":1,"title":"Book 1"},{"id":2,"title":"Book 2"},{"id":3,"title":"Book 3"}]' | jq -r '.taskUid')
  wait_task "$p" "$documents_task_uid"
done

echo "=== old version ==="
curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:${OLD_PORT}/version" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" | jq '{pkgVersion,commitSha}'
echo "=== new version ==="
curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:${NEW_PORT}/version" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" | jq '{pkgVersion,commitSha}'

echo "=== query: {\"q\":\"\",\"page\":1,\"hitsPerPage\":1} ==="
echo "--- old ---"
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${OLD_PORT}/indexes/books/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"q":"","page":1,"hitsPerPage":1}' | jq '{ids:(.hits|map(.id)),hitsCount:(.hits|length),totalHits,totalPages,page,hitsPerPage}'
echo "--- new ---"
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${NEW_PORT}/indexes/books/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"q":"","page":1,"hitsPerPage":1}' | jq '{ids:(.hits|map(.id)),hitsCount:(.hits|length),totalHits,totalPages,page,hitsPerPage}'

echo "=== query: {\"q\":\"\",\"page\":2,\"hitsPerPage\":1} ==="
echo "--- old ---"
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${OLD_PORT}/indexes/books/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"q":"","page":2,"hitsPerPage":1}' | jq '{ids:(.hits|map(.id)),hitsCount:(.hits|length),totalHits,totalPages,page,hitsPerPage}'
echo "--- new ---"
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${NEW_PORT}/indexes/books/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"q":"","page":2,"hitsPerPage":1}' | jq '{ids:(.hits|map(.id)),hitsCount:(.hits|length),totalHits,totalPages,page,hitsPerPage}'
```

## Versions

- Older behavior: `getmeili/meilisearch-enterprise:v1.46.0`
- Reproduced regression: `getmeili/meilisearch-enterprise:v1.48.3`

## Additional context

- This is the issue causing the [Rails SDK tests](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/actions/runs/28357202704/job/84002952924) to fail
- In the tested finite-pagination responses, `hits` stayed capped while only `totalHits` / `totalPages` changed.
- Relevant references:
  - Search API spec: https://specs.meilisearch.dev/specifications/text/0118-search-api.html
  - Pagination setting spec: https://specs.meilisearch.dev/specifications/text/157-pagination-setting-api.html
  - Pagination docs: https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/capabilities/full_text_search/how_to/paginate_search_results

> [!NOTE]
> The bug report is written with the assistance of Cursor and `gpt-5.4-high`

title: Embedder `dimensions=4097` accepted by settings API, exceeding documented max of 4096
body:
## Describe the bug

The settings API accepts embedder `dimensions` values above the documented maximum of 4096 without returning a validation error. While `dimensions=0` is correctly rejected with a 400, `dimensions=4097` returns 202 (accepted as async task) instead of being rejected synchronously.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an index:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"uid": "embedder-test"}'

# Wait for task to complete
```

2. Set `dimensions=0` (below min) — **correctly rejected**:

```bash
curl -X PATCH 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/embedder-test/settings' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"embedders": {"default": {"source": "userProvided", "dimensions": 0}}}'
```

Response (400):
```json
{"message":"`.embedders.default.dimensions`: `dimensions` cannot be zero","code":"invalid_settings_embedders","type":"invalid_request","link":"https://docs.meilisearch.com/errors#invalid_settings_embedders"}
```

3. Set `dimensions=4096` (max boundary) — **correctly accepted**:

```bash
curl -X PATCH 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/embedder-test/settings' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"embedders": {"default": {"source": "userProvided", "dimensions": 4096}}}'
```

Response (202):
```json
{"taskUid": 7, "status": "enqueued", "type": "settingsUpdate"}
```

4. Set `dimensions=4097` (above max) — **incorrectly accepted** (should be 400):

```bash
curl -X PATCH 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/embedder-test/settings' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"embedders": {"default": {"source": "userProvided", "dimensions": 4097}}}'
```

Response (202, should be 400):
```json
{"taskUid": 8, "status": "enqueued", "type": "settingsUpdate"}
```

## Expected behavior

Per the [embedders settings documentation](https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/settings/list-all-settings#embedders), `dimensions` must be bigger than zero and lower or equal to the chosen model's dimensions. For `userProvided` embedders with no external model, the API should enforce a reasonable upper bound synchronously. A value of 4097 should be rejected at validation level with a 400 error, consistent with how `dimensions=0` is handled.

For `userProvided` embedders, there is no external model to validate against, so the API-level range check should be the authoritative validation. Accepting the value as an async task that may fail later provides poor developer experience — the error is deferred and less actionable.

## Meilisearch version

v1.48.3

## Additional context

- The documentation notes dimensions range is `[1, 4096]` with a "depends on model" qualifier — but for `userProvided` source, no external model exists
- `dimensions=-1` is also accepted (202) despite being clearly invalid — the same validation gap applies to all out-of-range values above 0
- Running in development mode (`MEILI_ENV=development`, no master key)
- Docker image: `getmeili/meilisearch:v1.48.3`

title: Vector search returns 400 `missing_search_hybrid` despite `hybrid` documented as optional
body:
## Describe the bug

Performing a vector search with a correctly-dimensioned `vector` parameter (without `hybrid`) returns a 400 error `missing_search_hybrid`. This contradicts the official documentation and API contract, where `hybrid` is explicitly listed as an **optional** parameter and usage examples show vector search without it.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an index with a `userProvided` embedder (dimensions=4) and add a document:

```bash
# Create index
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"uid": "vector-test"}'

# Configure embedder
curl -X PATCH 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/vector-test/settings' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"embedders": {"default": {"source": "userProvided", "dimensions": 4}}}'

# Add document with vector
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/vector-test/documents' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '[{"id": 1, "title": "test", "_vectors": {"default": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]}}]'

# Wait for all tasks to complete
```

2. Search with correct vector dimension but **without** `hybrid` — returns 400:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/vector-test/search' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"q": "test", "vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]}'
```

Response:
```json
{
  "message": "Invalid request: missing `hybrid` parameter when `vector` or `media` are present.",
  "code": "missing_search_hybrid",
  "type": "invalid_request",
  "link": "https://docs.meilisearch.com/errors#missing_search_hybrid"
}
```

3. Adding `hybrid` makes it work (200), confirming the vector itself is valid:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/vector-test/search' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"q": "test", "vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "hybrid": {"embedder": "default"}}'
```

Response (200 with results):
```json
{"hits":[{"id":1,"title":"test"}],"estimatedTotalHits":1,"semanticHitCount":1}
```

## Expected behavior

Per the documentation, `hybrid` is an optional parameter for the search endpoint:

- The [Search API reference](https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/search) lists `hybrid` as optional: *"Hybrid search config (semanticRatio, embedder)"*
- The [user-provided embeddings guide](https://meilisearch.com/docs/learn/ai_powered_search/search_with_user_provided_embeddings) describes the `vector` parameter as mandatory for `userProvided` embedders, but does **not** state that `hybrid` becomes mandatory when `vector` is provided:

Either the documentation should be updated to clarify that `hybrid` is required when `vector` is used, or the API should accept `vector` without `hybrid` as documented.

## Meilisearch version

v1.48.3

## Additional context

- The error link `https://docs.meilisearch.com/errors#missing_search_hybrid` does not document this error code
- The `vector` parameter is correctly typed and dimensioned — the 400 is purely about the missing `hybrid` parameter
- Running in development mode (`MEILI_ENV=development`, no master key)
- Docker image: `getmeili/meilisearch:v1.48.3`

title: Typo tolerance `minWordSizeForTypos` settings have no effect on search results
body:
## Describe the bug

Configuring `typoTolerance.minWordSizeForTypos` to restrictive values has no observable effect on search results. A 4-character query that should be filtered out by the restrictive settings (requiring 10+ chars for one typo) still returns the same matches as with default settings, indicating the typo tolerance configuration is silently ignored.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an index and add documents with similar words:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"uid": "typo-test", "primaryKey": "id"}'

# Wait for task to complete, then add documents
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/typo-test/documents' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '[
    {"id": 1, "title": "apple pie recipe"},
    {"id": 2, "title": "application framework"},
    {"id": 3, "title": "appliance repair"}
  ]'

# Wait for task to complete
```

2. Search with query `"appl"` (4 chars) using **default** typo tolerance — returns 3 hits via prefix/typo matching:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/typo-test/search' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"q": "appl"}'
```

Response (3 hits):
```json
{"hits":[{"id":1,"title":"apple pie recipe"},{"id":2,"title":"application framework"},{"id":3,"title":"appliance repair"}],"estimatedTotalHits":3}
```

3. Set restrictive typo tolerance — `oneTypo=10` means words must be at least 10 chars to get any typo correction:

```bash
curl -X PATCH 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/typo-test/settings' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "typoTolerance": {
      "enabled": true,
      "minWordSizeForTypos": {"oneTypo": 10, "twoTypos": 20}
    }
  }'

# Wait for settings update task to complete (status=succeeded)
```

4. Search again with the same query `"appl"` — **identical results**, typo tolerance settings had no effect:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/typo-test/search' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"q": "appl"}'
```

Response (same 3 hits):
```json
{"hits":[{"id":1,"title":"apple pie recipe"},{"id":2,"title":"application framework"},{"id":3,"title":"appliance repair"}],"estimatedTotalHits":3}
```

## Expected behavior

With `minWordSizeForTypos.oneTypo=10`, a 4-character query `"appl"` should not trigger typo correction for the word `"apple"` (which differs by 1 typo but is only 5 chars, well below the 10-char threshold). The search results should differ from the default configuration — at minimum, `"apple pie recipe"` should not match `"appl"` via typo tolerance.

Per the [typo tolerance documentation](https://meilisearch.com/docs/capabilities/full_text_search/relevancy/typo_tolerance_settings#minwordsizefortypos), `minWordSizeForTypos` controls the minimum word length required before typo correction is applied:

> By default, Meilisearch accepts one typo for query terms containing five or more characters, and up to two typos if the term is at least nine characters long. You can override these default settings using the `minWordSizeForTypos` object.

Setting `oneTypo=10` should prevent typo correction on query words shorter than 10 characters. Since `"appl"` is only 4 characters, it should not receive any typo correction and thus should not match `"apple"` via a typo.

## Meilisearch version

v1.48.3

## Additional context

- The settings PATCH task completes successfully (task status `succeeded`), confirming the configuration was accepted by the server
- The issue is not specific to the `/settings` endpoint — using `/settings/typo-tolerance` produces the same result
- Running in development mode (`MEILI_ENV=development`, no master key)
- Docker image: `getmeili/meilisearch:v1.48.3`

title: fix(chats): keep streaming when a provider sends a choice-less chunk
body:
# Pull Request

## Related issue

Fixes #6341

## What does this PR do?

Chat completions stop producing any output against Azure OpenAI (and any
provider whose stream opens with a metadata-only chunk).

The streaming loop in `stream_chat_completion` reads each SSE chunk and does:

```rust
let choice = match resp.choices.first() {
    Some(choice) => choice,
    None => break,
};
```

Azure OpenAI opens the stream with a chunk that carries an **empty `choices`
array** (the prompt content-filter results), e.g.:

```jsonl
{"choices":[],"created":0,"id":"","model":"","object":"","prompt_filter_results":[{"prompt_index":0,"content_filter_results":{ ... }}]}
```

That leading chunk hits `None => break`, so the loop exits on the very first
chunk and the whole completion is aborted before any content is streamed back —
the reported "no responses are generated".

This PR skips choice-less chunks (`continue`) instead of treating them as the
end of the stream:

- The leading Azure prompt-filter chunk is skipped, and the subsequent content
  chunks are streamed normally.
- The trailing usage-only chunk (emitted when `include_usage` is set, also
  choice-less) is still accounted for by the `resp.usage` block just above the
  match; it is then skipped, and the stream ends naturally on the next `None`
  from `response.next()` — same outcome as before for the non-Azure path.

So there is no behavior change for OpenAI/Mistral/vLLM streams; the only
difference is that a choice-less chunk no longer kills an in-progress response.

## PR checklist

- The chat streaming path does not yet have an integration-test harness
  (tracked separately in #6179), so this was verified by tracing the code
  against the exact chunk sequence captured in the issue. Glad to add a
  mock-SSE regression test if you'd like one as part of this PR.

title: Bug Report - Mismatch Between Sidebar Counts and Search Results Grid
body:
# Bug Report - Mismatch Between Sidebar Counts and Search Results Grid

## Summary

An inconsistency has been identified in the hybrid search implementation of Meilisearch, where the product counts displayed in the sidebar filters do not match the number of products actually displayed in the search results grid.

The issue occurs because sidebar counts are calculated before the minimum relevance threshold is applied, while the grid only displays products that remain after this filtering process.

## Environment

* Search Engine: Meilisearch
* Search Type: Hybrid Search (Keyword Search + Semantic Search)

## Current Behavior

### Grid Calculation

When a customer searches for a term such as **"rugs"**, the search engine performs two searches simultaneously:

1. Text Search

   * Returns products containing the searched keyword in the product name, description, or indexed attributes.

2. Semantic Search

   * Returns products that are conceptually related to the searched term, even if they do not contain the exact keyword.

The results from both searches are combined into a single candidate list.

Each candidate receives a relevance score ranging from **0 to 1**.

Afterward, a quality threshold is applied:

* Minimum score required: **0.40**
* Products with a score below this threshold are discarded.

Only products that pass this threshold are displayed in the search results grid.

### Sidebar Calculation

The sidebar filter counts are generated from the same candidate list produced by the hybrid search.

However, these counts are calculated before the minimum relevance threshold is applied.

Current flow:

Candidate list generated
↓
Sidebar counts products
↓
Minimum relevance threshold (0.40) applied
↓
Grid displays remaining products

## Observed Behavior

### Example

Filter:

* 3 ALUNOS BA (4)

Displayed result:

* 0 products

### What Happens

The four products belonging to the "3 ALUNOS BA" category were considered related to the search term by the semantic search engine.

As a result:

* They were included in the sidebar count.
* They received relevance scores between 0.22 and 0.24.

Since the configured minimum relevance score is 0.40:

* All four products were removed from the final result set.
* No products were displayed in the grid.

Final outcome:

* Sidebar displays 4 products.
* Grid displays 0 products.

## Expected Behavior

The counts displayed in the sidebar filters should accurately reflect the number of products that are eligible to appear in the search results grid after all relevance rules and thresholds have been applied.

Example:

* If no products within a category meet the minimum relevance score of 0.40, the sidebar should display a count of 0 for that category.

## Impact

* Inconsistent user experience.
* Potential confusion during navigation and filtering.
* Users may believe products are available within a filter when selecting it ultimately returns an empty result set.
* Reduced trust in search accuracy.

## Root Cause

The sidebar and the search results grid use the same candidate set but at different stages of the search pipeline:

* Sidebar → calculated before the relevance threshold is applied.
* Grid → calculated after the relevance threshold is applied.

This discrepancy results in facet counts that may include products that are later removed from the displayed search results.

## Status

Confirmed bug.

The root cause has been identified as a known behavior of Meilisearch Hybrid Search, where facet counts can be calculated from the candidate set before the relevance threshold is applied to the final displayed results.

title: Fix S3 Snapshots race condition when trying to recycle buffers
body:
This PR fixes [a known tokio issue](https://github.com/tokio-rs/bytes/issues/350) where an async task using [Bytes](https://docs.rs/bytes/latest/bytes/struct.Bytes.html) would finish, and another task is trying to recycle the borrowed Bytes from this task [to convert them into BytesMut ones](https://docs.rs/bytes/latest/bytes/struct.Bytes.html#method.try_into_mut), and the original Bytes are not yet dropped, so there is still a reference to them, and the conversion fails. In this particularly rare case, we decide to allocate a new buffer instead.

title: Split unit tests into separate files (one commit per file)
body:
## Related issue

Part of #5116

## What does this PR do?

Several files carry hundreds (or thousands) of lines of unit tests at the end of the source file, which slows down rust-analyzer and makes the modules harder to navigate.

This PR moves the trailing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block out of each source file into a sibling test file, following the convention already used in the codebase (`option_test.rs`, `search/mod_test.rs`, `autobatcher_test.rs`). **One commit per file**, as requested:

1. `milli` — `update/index_documents/mod.rs` → `mod_test.rs`
2. `milli` — `search/new/matches/mod.rs` → `mod_test.rs`
3. `milli` — `update/facet/incremental.rs` → `incremental_test.rs`
4. `milli` — `search/facet/facet_range_search.rs` → `facet_range_search_test.rs`
5. `permissive-json-pointer` — `lib.rs` → `lib_test.rs`

Notes:
- For plain-file modules (`incremental.rs`, `facet_range_search.rs`) the new module is declared in the parent `mod.rs` and `use super::...` imports are adjusted accordingly.
- File-based (`milli_snap` / `db_snap!`) snapshot directories are renamed to match the new source file names; inline snapshots need no change.
- No test logic is changed.

`cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` all pass.

This replaces the earlier separate PRs (#6453, #6460, #6461, #6464, #6465), consolidated here into a single PR with one commit per file. Apologies again for the earlier noise.

title: Improve the synonyms storage
body:
This PR improves how we store synonyms, so users can store many more without impacting performance, and will no longer be advised to store keywords in documents instead of using synonyms.

### Changelog

We improve synonyms' performance by changing how we store and retrieve them during query processing. Users may have experienced performance issues when the number of synonyms in an index was high, significantly impacting search performance. The Meilisearch support team advised moving the settings and synonyms-as-keywords to the dedicated documents. This is no longer an issue; synonyms are loaded lazily, only when a word matches a synonym. You can see performance improvements of up to 13x, depending on the number of synonyms.

## To Do
 - [x] Introduce a dumpless upgrade to migrate synonyms to the new dedicated database.
	 - [x] Make sure the version is the right one
 - [x] Use the tokenizer to normalize and split associated synonyms.
 - [x] Reduce the number of allocations.
 - [x] Remove the original key from the new synonyms DB
 - [x] Improve the workload test to show the issue with the dumpless upgrade
 - [x] Benchmark and show actual numbers

## Small benchmarks

Testing with Meilisearch v1.48.3 with 15k synonyms.

```json
"performanceDetails": {
    "wait in queue": "51.00µs",
    "search > partition queries": "61.88µs",
    "search > start remote search": "59.92µs",
    "search > execute local search > tokenize query": "6.18ms",
    "search > execute local search > evaluate query": "166.25µs",
    "search > execute local search > keyword ranking": "192.54µs",
    "search > execute local search > format": "31.04µs",
    "search > execute local search": "13.20ms",
    "search > wait for remote results": "20.17µs",
    "search > merge results": "44.21µs",
    "search > hydrate documents": "46.42µs",
    "search > merge facets": "10.63µs",
    "search": "13.51ms"
}
```

Testing with this PR and still 15k synonyms. Basically 13x faster.

```json
"performanceDetails": {
    "wait in queue": "80.46µs",
    "search > partition queries": "46.00µs",
    "search > start remote search": "67.83µs",
    "search > execute local search > tokenize query": "123.04µs",
    "search > execute local search > evaluate query": "221.50µs",
    "search > execute local search > keyword ranking": "191.00µs",
    "search > execute local search > format": "18.92µs",
    "search > execute local search": "1.01ms",
    "search > wait for remote results": "27.21µs",
    "search > merge results": "40.75µs",
    "search > hydrate documents": "24.38µs",
    "search > merge facets": "12.83µs",
    "search": "1.27ms"
}
```

## This PR makes breaking changes

*Breaking changes are changes to the database such that databases created in an older version of Meilisearch need changes to remain valid in the new version of Meilisearch. This typically happens when the way data is stored changes (change of database, new required key, etc.). This can also happen due to breaking changes in the API of an experimental feature. ⚠️ These kinds of changes are more difficult to achieve safely, so proceed with caution and test the dumpless upgrade right before merging the PR.*

- [x] Detail the changes to the DB format,
    - [x] which are not compatible, why, and how they will be fixed up in the upgrade
			We changed how we store synonyms. Instead of storing them in a large JSON object that must be fully deserialized in RAM when querying the engine, we store the synonyms in a dedicated database, with each entry containing the key and its associated value. This allows us to query only the interesting synonyms on demand and avoid unnecessary deserializations.
 - [ ] ❌ Ensure all the read operations still work!
     We decided it would be easier to avoid reading the previous version of the synonyms (stored in a single large object) and wait for the dumpless upgrade to finish migrating them to the new dedicated database. The impact is that synonyms will not be applied when the migration is not done. Migrations are pretty quick, the impact is therefore minimal, and the amount of code to maintain is way smaller.
  - [x] Write the code to go from the old database to the new one
    - [x] If the change happened in milli, the upgrade function should be written and called [here](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/3fd86e8d76d7d468b0095d679adb09211ca3b6c0/crates/milli/src/update/upgrade/mod.rs#L24-L47)
  - [x] Declarative test: add a [declarative test containing a dumpless upgrade](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/TESTING.md#typical-usage)
	 I decided to change the movies.json workload to introduce synonyms and demonstrate that synonyms are not visible for a short time while the dumpless upgrade is in progress and available just after it's complete.
