title: Tool calls and/or internal reasoning appear as plaintext of chat responses
body:
## Describe the bug

We're seeing a recurring issue with the chat completions endpoint, where the assistant response includes internals that are not supposed to be user-facing. In particular:

- A JSON object that looks similar to tool calls is included in the text output, before the actual response.
- Text that looks like reasoning tokens.

We use the `openai` provider and the `gpt-5.4` model at the moment, though we saw the same error with other models as well.

## JSON objects

Sometimes we get JSON in the text output (`chunk.choices[0].delta.content`), before the actual response.

For example (formatted for readability, the actual output doesn't include any whitespace):

```json
{
    "tool_uses": [
        {
            "recipient_name": "functions._meiliSearchInIndex",
            "parameters": {
                "index_uid": "pages",
                "q": "Stipendien Baden-Württemberg",
                "filter": ""
            }
        },
        {
            "recipient_name": "functions._meiliSearchInIndex",
            "parameters": {
                "index_uid": "pages",
                "q": "",
                "filter": "id = 840027"
            }
        },
        {
            "recipient_name": "functions._meiliSearchInIndex",
            "parameters": {
                "index_uid": "offers",
                "q": "Stipendium",
                "filter": "audience = 'Grundschüler/in' AND type_foerderangebote = 'Stipendium'"
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

After that, the model returns a newline and then the actual response for the user.

This is weird, because this output isn't a documented behavior of the model or the Chat Completions API. It's not how the model is supposed to do tool calls. It _may_ just be an error of the model, but we haven't seen anything like this when calling the OpenAI API directly. I think it's most likely an error in Meilisearch's handling of the response, or in the `async-openai` fork.

### Internal monologue in the output

Sometimes the message starts with an internal monologue of the model, similar to the reasoning tokens that you see in ChatGPT or Copilot. There are two "tells" that this is happening:

- The model is talking about itself in the first person ("I should search for XYZ …")
- The text reads like a stream of consciousness rather than a response ("Should I do XYZ now?", "I could use `q` and `filter` XYZ …").

The assistant is only for a German audience, so here's a German example:

> Ich brauche eine Rückfrage: Für Stipendien soll ich nicht nach Ort fragen, aber zusätzlich nach dem Bundesland fragen; das hat der Nutzer schon genannt. Ich sollte jetzt nach Zielgruppe/Fokus fragen? Für Stipendienregel: suche ohne Ort, pages nach "Stipendien Baden-Württemberg" und verweise auf Beitrag "Stipendium" im Index pages. Außerdem reguläre Suche plus Sonderregel? Keine spezielle Sonderregel für Stipendium. Da Anfrage nach passendem Stipendium für 4. Klasse, wohl Zielgruppe Grundschule. Ich kann wohl direkt suchen: offers q "Stipendium" filter audience IN ['Grundschüler/in','Schüler/in']? und pages q "Stipendien Baden-Württemberg", plus pages q "Stipendium".Ich habe nach Stipendien für Baden-Württemberg geschaut. Für die 4. Klasse finde ich in der Datenbank kein klar passendes Einzelstipendium.

Here's an automated translation:

> I need a follow-up question: For scholarships I should not ask about location, but additionally ask about the federal state; the user has already mentioned it. I should now ask about target group/focus? For scholarship rule: search without location, pages for "Stipendien Baden-Württemberg" and refer to article "Stipendium" in the pages index. Also regular search plus special rule? No special rule for Stipendium. Since request is for a suitable scholarship for 4th grade, probably target group elementary school. I can probably search directly: offers q "Stipendium" filter audience IN ['Grundschüler/in','Schüler/in']? and pages q "Stipendien Baden-Württemberg", plus pages q "Stipendium".I have looked for scholarships for Baden-Württemberg. For 4th grade I find no clearly matching individual scholarship in the database.

**Very important:** You can tell where the reasoning/internal monologue ends and the actual response starts because there's no space between it here:

> … plus pages q "Stipendium".I have looked for scholarships … 

Again, could be a model issue, but we haven't seen anything like this except with Meilisearch chat completions. So I assume that there's an issue with Meilisearch's handling of the response.

## Suggested fix

I think the best solution would be to switch to the Responses API. The Chat completions API is already soft-deprecated and apparently, doesn't work well with reasoning models.

---

I had Claude analyse what might cause this in the current implementation. I'm posting this as a starting point, but I can't independently verify if this assessment is correct.

## Possible causes (AI-generated speculation)

Both symptoms share the same root: [`forward_response`](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/crates/meilisearch/src/routes/chats/utils.rs) is a thin pass-through — it serialises the raw upstream chunk and writes it to the SSE stream with no content filtering whatsoever.

The `run_conversation` loop in `chat_completions.rs` dispatches on `delta.tool_calls`:

- `Some(tool_calls)` → accumulate streaming tool-call chunks, do **not** forward content.
- `None` → if there are pending Meilisearch calls, resolve them; otherwise call `forward_response`.

When the model outputs tool invocations as plain JSON in `delta.content` instead of using the native `tool_calls` field, the `None` branch fires and the raw JSON is forwarded to the client as regular assistant text.

The JSON shape in the bug report (`{"tool_uses":[{"recipient_name":"functions._meiliSearchInIndex",…}]}`) is a text-based function-calling format that some models fall back to when they don't recognise (or don't correctly follow) the structured `tool_calls` API. The `functions.` prefix in `recipient_name` is characteristic of this fallback behaviour. This means Meilisearch never intercepts the calls, never runs the searches, and instead leaks the raw invocation JSON to the end user.

## Meilisearch version

1.29.0

title: fix(chats): avoid internal error on chat completions against empty index
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5808.

When a chat completions request hits an index that has never had documents indexed, `format_documents` calls `index.external_id_of(...)`, which unconditionally reads the primary key from the main database before iterating over document IDs. On an empty index, no primary key has been set, so `ok_or(InternalError::DatabaseMissingEntry { ... })` fires and the client receives:

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "code": "500",
    "message": "internal: missing primary-key in the main database."
  }
}
```

This error is emitted before the chat stream continues, which is both confusing and incorrect — an empty result set is perfectly valid.

## Fix

Early-return `Ok(Vec::new())` in `format_documents` when `internal_docids` is empty. No documents to render means no document IDs to look up, and no primary key is needed. This matches the intent of the `external_id_of` precondition comment ("never called on an empty index") while making the call site safe for the zero-results case.

The change is 5 lines in `crates/meilisearch/src/routes/chats/utils.rs`.

title: fix(auth): re-expand wildcard key actions at lookup for post-creation actions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5691.

Keys created with `Action::All` (or any group wildcard like `Action::ChatsAll`) have their actions expanded at creation time via `enum_iterator::all::<Action>()` and stored in an inverted DB. After a dumpless upgrade that introduces new leaf actions (e.g. `ChatsGet`, `ChatsDelete` added after a key was created), those keys never receive the new actions in the inverted DB and silently cannot use the new features.

### Root cause

`put_api_key` snapshots `enum_iterator::all::<Action>()` at write time. The inverted DB entry for a new action is never created retroactively, so `get_expiration_date` / `prefix_first_expiration_date` return `None` → `is_key_authorized` returns `false`.

### Fix

**Extract `expand_actions(&[Action]) -> HashSet<Action>`** from `put_api_key` (no behavioural change at creation time) and call it as a runtime fallback in both lookup functions:

1. `get_expiration_date` — when the inverted DB returns `None`, look up the stored `Key` and re-expand its `actions` slice against the *current* `Action` enum. If the requested action is now covered and the key's index patterns permit the requested index, return `key.expires_at`.
2. `prefix_first_expiration_date` — same fallback when the prefix scan returns nothing.

Index restrictions are fully honoured in the fallback path (`IndexUidPattern::matches_all` / `matches_str`). Expiration dates from the stored key are respected.

## Tests

Two new unit tests in `store::tests`:

title: Clamp single-index map_size to the page size in index_budget
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #6233 (and removes one cause of #6051).

## What does this PR do?

In `index_budget()` (`crates/index-scheduler/src/lib.rs`), the `index_count < 2` branch built its `map_size` as:

```rust
let map_size = (budget * 2) / 5;
```

without aligning it to the page size. The two sibling budget paths in the same function both clamp (`task_db_size = clamp_to_page_size(budget * 2 / 5)` and the `>= 2` path returns the already-clamped `base_map_size`). On platforms with a larger page size (Windows, 4096 bytes), `heed` rejects an unaligned `map_size`, so the single-index budget path could produce a value that fails to open — the snapshot failure reported in #6051.

Wrapping the value in `clamp_to_page_size()` makes this path consistent with the other two:

```rust
let map_size = clamp_to_page_size((budget * 2) / 5);
```

`clamp_to_page_size` is already imported in this module. No behavior change on platforms where the value was already aligned.

## Requirements

- [ ] Automated tests have been added.
  - `index_budget` is a private associated function with no existing unit test; its `index_count < 2` branch only triggers when `base_map_size` is large relative to the discovered budget, and reaching it in a test requires opening a real (multi-TiB) `heed` env. This change mirrors the two already-clamped sibling paths in the same function, so it carries no new behavior to assert beyond page alignment. Happy to add a targeted test if you'd prefer one.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p index-scheduler` and `cargo fmt -- --check` pass locally.

title: Add dumpless-upgrade orchestration test on a user-populated database
body:
## Related issue

Addresses #5392.

This is a partial step toward the issue — see [Scope](#scope) below for what is and isn't covered.

## What this PR adds

One new integration test in `crates/meilisearch/tests/upgrade/mod.rs`:

```
dumpless_upgrade_from_v1_12_with_local_db
```

It exercises the dumpless-upgrade orchestration end-to-end without depending on a checked-in `.ms` fixture:

1. Boots a server with the current binary, creates an index, updates settings (`searchableAttributes`, `filterableAttributes`, `sortableAttributes`) and adds two documents — waits for every task to succeed.
2. Copies the populated database into a fresh tempdir and overwrites the `VERSION` file with `1.12.0`. The copy step sidesteps re-opening the same LMDB env twice in the same process.
3. Boots a second server on the new tempdir with `experimental_dumpless_upgrade: true` and asserts that:
   - the `VERSION` file is rewritten to the current binary version,
   - an `upgradeDatabase` task is auto-enqueued with `details.upgradeFrom = "v1.12.0"` and succeeds,
   - the user's index, settings (all three attribute lists) and documents survive,
   - a sort+filter search returns the expected hit (`age >= 5` → `kefir`),
   - the original two task uids (`0 = settingsUpdate`, `1 = documentAdditionOrUpdate`) remain queryable.

## Why `from = 1.12.0`

While picking a `from` version I noticed anything other than 1.12.0 silently no-ops. `update_version_file_for_dumpless_upgrade` (in `crates/meilisearch/src/lib.rs`) only syncs the index-scheduler's internal version DB on the `from_minor == 12` branch — that's the entry `upgrade_index_scheduler` reads to decide whether to run migrations. For any later `from`, the internal version is left at the current binary, so `upgrade_index_scheduler` early-returns at `initial_version == target_version` and no upgrade task is ever enqueued. Picking 1.12.0 is what actually fires the migration pipeline. There's also a doc comment on the test calling this out for future readers.

## Scope

This is an **orchestration** test on a current-format database — it verifies the `check_version → update_version_file_for_dumpless_upgrade → Versioning::new → upgrade_index_scheduler → UpgradeDatabase task` chain works end-to-end and preserves user data. It is **not** a real format-migration test: the underlying LMDB bytes were written by the current binary, so the per-version migration functions run but have no meaningful format work to do.

Real format migration is already covered by the existing `crates/meilisearch/tests/upgrade/v1_12/v1_12_0.rs` test, which loads a checked-in v1.12.0 database fixture. The new test complements that one — it adds coverage for the orchestration on a user-populated DB, which the static-fixture test can't (its DB is a fixed reference).

A follow-up PR could add a real fixture for a more recent starting version (e.g. v1.45.0) once someone with the previous-version binary available can generate and commit the `.ms` directory.

## Test plan

Local (Rust 1.91.1, macOS):

- `cargo test -p meilisearch --test integration upgrade` — all 6 upgrade tests pass (4 pre-existing in `mod.rs` + `import_v1_12_0` + the new test).
- `cargo clippy -p meilisearch --tests -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo fmt -- --check crates/meilisearch/tests/upgrade/mod.rs` — clean. (Pre-existing fmt diff in `crates/meilisearch/tests/upgrade/v1_12/v1_12_0.rs:7` exists on `main` too — not touched.)

title: [Experimental] Only support foreign filters on retrieval routes
body:
## Related issue

related to https://linear.app/meilisearch/issue/EXP-1027

## Generative AI tools

- [x] This PR does not use generative AI tooling

## Note for the reviewer

The goal of this PR is to prepare the field for sharding support.
Most of the writing routes have their logic at the index-scheduler level, but the proxy logic is at meilisearch(-http) level.
This means that:
- either we move all the proxy/sharding logic to a level accessible to the index scheduler
- either we forbid the usage of the foreign filter for the writing routes

We chose to forbid the foreign filter in the writing routes for now.

## Changelog

Foreign filters are meant to be used in a retrieval context (search, get document...), but all the actions related to writing or modifying a document could have several unexpected behaviors if foreign filters are accepted.
We prefer forbidding the usage of this feature on the writing routes.

The following routes do not support Foreign-filter anymore:
- [Edit documents by function](https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/documents/edit-documents-by-function): POST `/indexes/{index_uid}/documents/edit`
- [Delete documents by filter](https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/documents/delete-documents-by-filter): POST `/indexes/{index_uid}/documents/delete`
- [Export to a remote Meilisearch](https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/export/export-to-a-remote-meilisearch): POST `/export`

Additional change: we now ensure that the experimental features are checked when parsing a filter

title: fix(milli): support prefix search on disableOnAttributes and disableOnNumbers fields
body:
## Summary

Fixes [#6403](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/6403).

When `typoTolerance.disableOnAttributes` or `disableOnNumbers` is enabled, matching tokens are stored in `exact_word_docids` instead of `word_docids`. Prefix search still worked on tolerant fields (e.g. query `ma` → `many` in `content`), but failed on exact fields (e.g. query `hel` → `Hello` in `title`) once prefix databases were built at indexing time.

## Root cause

Prefix post-processing only tracked changes from `word_docids` (`WordDelta`). Words that exist solely in `exact_word_docids` were never:

1. Registered in the prefix FST builder during indexing
2. Passed to `compute_exact_word_prefix_docids`

So `exact_word_prefix_docids` stayed empty for prefixes like `hel`, while tolerant prefixes like `ma` were populated correctly.

## What changed

- Track an **exact word delta** alongside the existing word delta during document/settings extraction
- Register exact-word additions/deletions in the prefix FST (without adding them to the tolerant `words_fst`)
- Compute prefix databases separately:
  - `word_prefix_docids` ← tolerant word changes
  - `exact_word_prefix_docids` ← exact word changes
  - `word_prefix_fid_docids` / `word_prefix_position_docids` ← union of both (field data already contains exact words)
- Mirror `disableOnNumbers` FST migration for the new exact-word delta path

## Behavior preserved

- Typo tolerance remains disabled on configured attributes/numbers (no change to ranking or typo rules)
- Prefix search remains disabled when `prefixSearch` is `disabled`
- Existing tolerant-field prefix behavior is unchanged

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_prefix_search_on_exact_attribute_and_disable_on_numbers` in `crates/milli/src/search/new/tests/typo.rs`
  - 100 documents with `title` (exact) + `content` (tolerant)
  - Asserts `ma` and `hel` prefix queries both return hits
- [x] `cargo test -p milli test_prefix_search_on_exact_attribute_and_disable_on_numbers`

## Requirements

- [x] Automated tests added
- [x] No database schema change (`no db change`)
- [x] This PR does not use generative AI tooling for the implementation *(author used Cursor for development — disclosed per contributing guidelines)*

## Related

- Issue reported from settings indexer work in #6398
- User-facing setting: `typoTolerance.disableOnAttributes` / `disableOnNumbers` ([docs](https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/learn/relevancy/typo_tolerance))

title: perf(tracing): add missing trace spans to facet bulk post-processing
body:
Closes #5654

## Problem

The three functions in `crates/milli/src/update/new/indexer/post_processing/facet_bulk.rs` had no tracing instrumentation:

- `generate_facet_levels` — called once per filterable field in bulk mode
- `compute_level` — called once per level while building the facet hierarchy  
- `clear_levels` — clears existing levels before rebuilding

This meant ~6 seconds of bulk facet post-processing time was invisible in profiling traces (puffin / tracing spans), making it impossible to attribute time to individual field IDs or hierarchy levels.

## Fix

Add `#[tracing::instrument]` to all three functions with relevant fields:

| Function | Fields |
|---|---|
| `generate_facet_levels` | `field_id`, `facet_type` |
| `compute_level` | `field_id`, `base_level` |
| `clear_levels` | `field_id` |

The spans use `level = "trace"` and `target = "indexing::post_processing::facet_bulk"` consistent with the existing instrumentation in `mod.rs`.

## Testing

`cargo check -p milli` passes. No logic was changed — tracing attributes only.

title: Bump actions/github-script from 7 to 9
body:
Bumps [actions/github-script](https://github.com/actions/github-script) from 7 to 9.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/github-script's releases.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.
  • Orchestration ID in user-agent — The ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

Breaking changes:

  • require('@actions/github') no longer works in scripts. The upgrade to @actions/github v9 (ESM-only) means require('@actions/github') will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
  • getOctokit is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.
  • If your script accesses other @actions/github internals beyond the standard github/octokit client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

```json
{
  "legacySearch": true
}
```

available values:
- `true`: force old implementation
- `false`: force new implementation	
- `null`: use the instance default value

#### Set the instance default value for legacy search

This PR addresses a subtle but important issue with how Meilisearch handles termination signals in Docker. By using the shell form for `CMD`, the process was being wrapped by `/bin/sh`, which often doesn't forward `SIGTERM` to the underlying application. Switching to the exec form ensures `tini` can correctly manage the lifecycle of the binary, preventing potential LMDB corruption during unexpected container stops.

Additionally, an unused `apkArch` variable in the compiler stage has been removed to keep the Dockerfile clean.

These changes should be completely transparent to existing users while improving overall reliability.
author: RinZ27

title: Discussion: Official support for rootless Docker images
body:
**Describe the bug**
Currently, the official Meilisearch Dockerfile does not specify a non-root user. While this works fine for most setups, it forces the engine to run with elevated privileges inside the container, which goes against the principle of least privilege.

**Expected behavior**
Meilisearch should ideally run as a dedicated `meilisearch` user. This would provide an extra layer of defense-in-depth, especially since the engine handles sensitive data and is often exposed to the network.

**Additional context**
Implementing this requires careful consideration of volume permissions. If we simply add a `USER` instruction, existing users might face permission denied errors on their `/meili_data` volumes due to UID/GID mismatches.

Because of these potential breaking changes, opening a discussion first seemed more appropriate than just pushing a PR. Some options worth considering:
1. Providing a separate `-rootless` tag.
2. Updating the documentation to guide users through the `chown` process.
3. Using an entrypoint script that handles permission adjustment if run as root, then drops privileges.

Moving toward a rootless default would significantly improve the security posture of the official image for production environments.

title: fix: return task documents as valid ndjson

## Summary
- write converted JSON and CSV document payloads as newline-delimited JSON records
- keep `/tasks/{taskUid}/documents` aligned with its `application/x-ndjson` response type
- add regression coverage for the document formatter and the task documents endpoint

JSON and CSV uploads were converted into the task update file by writing each JSON object back-to-back without a separator. The task documents endpoint serves that file as `application/x-ndjson`, so JSON-array uploads could return bodies like `{...}{...}`, which are not valid NDJSON.

title: Promote dynamic search rules to index
body:
## Description
This PR reworks dynamic search rules so they are stored and queried through a dedicated internal Meilisearch index instead of a scheduler-owned key-value database plus an in-memory runtime map.

## Changelog
This is mostly an internal architecture change. The goal is to make dynamic search rules more scalable and to prepare the feature for future activation conditions, especially filter-based conditions, by relying on the same primitives Meilisearch already uses for indexed lookup rather than repeatedly scanning all rules.

At a high level, this change:

* Promotes dynamic search rules to documents in a hidden internal index managed by the index scheduler.
* Keeps the public DSR API unchanged while introducing an index-friendly internal representation.
* Configures the internal index with searchable, filterable, and sortable fields needed to list rules and resolve search-time candidates.
* Moves rule candidate resolution into the index scheduler so search only receives rules that are relevant for the current index/query context.
* Preserves rule behavior for priority, pin deduplication, time windows, query-empty/query-contains conditions, and global vs index-scoped actions.
* Simplifies the search-side dynamic rules code so it focuses on applying already-selected pinning actions.
* Updates dumps and route handling to read DSRs from the new store.
* Support filter-based activation conditions.

## Breaking change
This PR doesn't import previously created DSRs. They need to be created again.

title: Environment variable to configure max open indexes
body:
Problem

Currently, Meilisearch limits the number of simultaneously open indexes using an LRU cache (see crates/index-scheduler/src/index_mapper/). The default limit is:
- 20 indexes on Linux (based on typical ~256 file descriptor limit)
- 4 indexes on Windows

This is hardcoded in crates/meilisearch/src/lib.rs:68-94:

#[cfg(not(windows))]
const DEFAULT_INDEX_COUNT: usize = 20;

This creates a problem for users with thousands of indexes that are rarely used - they hit the 20-index limit and indexes must be constantly reopened, causing performance issues.

Proposed Solution

Add an environment variable to allow users to configure the max number of open indexes. Following the existing pattern for MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_INDEX_MAX_READERS (in index_map.rs:322), I suggest:

MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_INDEX_COUNT (or MEILI_INDEX_COUNT)

Implementation Notes

1. Read the env var in crates/meilisearch/src/lib.rs where IndexSchedulerOptions is constructed (around line 278)
2. Pass the value to IndexSchedulerOptions.index_count
3. Consider increasing the default if ulimit -n is higher than 256 (optional enhancement)

Workaround

Users can currently work around this by:
1. Increasing file descriptors with ulimit -n before starting the server
2. The LRU cache will then use more slots based on memory calculations in index_budget() at lib.rs:406-456

Thanks for your consideration.

title: index_budget() missing clamp_to_page_size for map_size when index_count < 2
body:
Hi there,

I was looking into the Windows snapshot issue (#6051) and noticed that in `index_budget()` (crates/index-scheduler/src/lib.rs), the `map_size` computation on the `index_count < 2` path doesn't use `clamp_to_page_size()`:

```rust
let map_size = (budget * 2) / 5;
```

The other two code paths in the same function (lines ~429 and ~461) both clamp the result to the page size, but this one doesn't. On Windows where the page size is 4096 bytes, the unaligned value causes heed to reject the map size.

I think wrapping it with `clamp_to_page_size()` should fix it — happy to submit a PR.

title: Panic while adding `userProvided` embedder setting on index
body:
**Describe the bug**
We're experiencing panics while updating indexes already containing documents with `userProvided` embedder. The issue happens sporadically and we're unable to reproduce it locally.

The process:
- update existing index with latest settings - searchable, filterable, no embedders
- synchronously reindex all documents in batches with default vector value
- separately update documents with real vector values generated with OpenAI as each batch finishes - these batches run concurrently with each other and previous step but only for already reindexed documents
- after all documents are reindexed and vectors updated delete records which were not reindexed as they're considered stale
- update index settings with `userProvided` embedder -> this steps panics

title: 500 error when deleting temporary index after swap_indexes (Python SDK / remote instance)
body:
**Describe the bug**
When I use the Meilisearch Python SDK to rebuild an index via a temporary index + `swap_indexes`, the deletion of the temporary index right after the swap consistently fails with a generic internal error: `{'status_code': 500, 'code': None, 'link': None, 'type': None, 'message': 'An unexpected error occurred'}`.

If I comment out the `swap_indexes` call, the delete succeeds.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use a remote Meilisearch instance (not local) and the Meilisearch Python SDK.
2. Create a temporary index (e.g. `products_tmp`).
3. Add all documents to the temporary index.
4. Perform an index swap between the temp index and the “live” index using `swap_indexes`.
5. Wait for the swap task to complete using `wait_for_task`.
6. Delete the temporary index.
7. Observe the error (500 / “An unexpected error occurred”) on the delete step.

Minimal code sketch:
```python
task = client.swap_indexes([("products_tmp", "products")])
if task:
    client.wait_for_task(task.task_uid)

client.index("products_tmp").delete()
```

Notes:
- I also tried adding an extra `sleep(5)` after the swap task finished, but the delete still fails.
- If I skip `swap_indexes`, `delete()` works normally.

**Expected behavior**
After `swap_indexes` completes (task finished), deleting the temporary index should succeed without returning a 500 error.

**Meilisearch version:**
Meilisearch server version: v1.15.2
Python SDK version: meilisearch==0.40.0

**Additional context**
- This runs inside a Django management command (`from django.core.management import BaseCommand`) that rebuilds the search index because I don’t know which products changed in the project database.
- Workflow:
  1) Create temporary index  
  2) Insert all documents  
  3) `swap_indexes` temporary <-> live  
  4) Remove temporary index  
- Meilisearch server is remote.
- If there is a recommended way to safely delete the swapped-out index (or additional tasks/events to wait for besides the swap task), guidance would be appreciated.

title: Add _geo_list support for multiple geo points per document
body:
## Summary

Adds `_geo_list` as a new reserved field allowing **multiple discrete geo points** per document — e.g., a company with multiple office locations, or a category aggregating all shop locations.

This addresses the use case described in https://github.com/orgs/meilisearch/discussions/508, and specifically fills the **sorting gap** left by the `_geojson` prototype (`prototype-cellulite-1`), which supports filtering but not distance-based sorting.

### What `_geo_list` provides

- **Field format:** `"_geo_list": [{"lat": 48.8, "lng": 2.3}, {"lat": 51.5, "lng": -0.1}, ...]`
- **Filtering:** `_geoRadius` and `_geoBoundingBox` match a document if **any** point in its `_geo_list` is within range
- **Sorting:** `_geoPoint(lat,lng):asc/desc` sorts by the **closest** (or farthest) point per document
- **Results:** `_geoDistance` reflects the minimum distance across both `_geo` and `_geo_list` points
- **Settings:** Add `"_geo_list"` to `filterableAttributes` / `sortableAttributes` (same pattern as `_geo`)

### Architecture

`_geo_list` shares the **same RTree and faceted bitmap** as `_geo`, avoiding infrastructure duplication:
- Multiple RTree entries per docid are structurally valid (`GeoPoint` stores `(DocumentId, [f64; 2])`)
- Sorting uses docid deduplication via `HashSet` in `fill_cache()` — the RTree's nearest-neighbor iterator guarantees the first hit per docid is the closest
- `_geoBoundingBox` uses an RTree-based query for `_geo_list` to avoid false positives from independent lat/lng facet pairing
- A `rebuild_geo_rtree()` function handles the "Documents → Settings" flow, rebuilding the RTree from scratch when geo settings change

## Changes (22 files, +1366 / -68)

1. **Constants, errors, Document trait** — `_geo_list` reserved field, `GeoListError` enum, `geo_list_field()` on Document trait + all implementations
2. **Settings and index methods** — `is_geo_list_*_enabled()`, `has_geo_list()`, `geo_list_fields_ids`, `run_geo_indexing()` in reindex trigger
3. **Extraction pipeline** — `extract_geo_list_coordinates()`, extended `GeoExtractor` to process `_geo_list` for insertions/updates/deletions
4. **Merger** — Fixed bitmap arithmetic for multi-point documents (a docid can appear in both removed and inserted sets)
5. **Facet extraction** — `extract_geo_list_document()` for `_geo_list.lat`/`_geo_list.lng` facet values
6. **Filtering** — `_geoRadius`/`_geoBoundingBox` extended; RTree-based bounding box query for `_geo_list` avoids false positives
7. **Sorting** — Docid deduplication in both ascending and descending RTree paths; `rebuild_geo_rtree()` for settings changes
8. **Search results** — `insert_geo_distance()` extended to consider `_geo_list` points
9. **17 integration tests** covering filtering, sorting, `_geoDistance`, document lifecycle, mixed `_geo`+`_geo_list`, edge cases, and settings changes

## Test plan

- [x] All 22 geo tests pass (17 new + 5 existing)
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- --deny warnings` clean
- [ ] Full CI suite

## Related

- Discussion: https://github.com/orgs/meilisearch/discussions/508
- GeoJSON prototype: #5758 (supports filtering but not sorting for multi-point documents)

title: Changing ranking rules order removes hits
body:
Hi,

I see that changing the order of ranking rules not only changes the order of hits, but also removes some of them. Is it expected?

In order to reproduce with Meilisearch v1.36, it is enough to:

1. create a brand new index with default settings, 
2. push the [prizes.json](https://github.com/meilisearch/demos/blob/main/src/nobel-prizes/setup/prizes.json) file,
3. run a simple query (e.g. "albert physics") and count hits,
4. change the ranking rules order (for instance, by moving the `attributeRank` rule to the top),
5. re-run the sample simple query as in step 3 and count hits again.

I get 8 hits for "albert physics" if using the default ranking rule order (namely `["words", "typo", "proximity", "attributeRank", "sort", "wordPosition", "exactness"]`, only 3 hits if ranking rules are ordered as follows: `["attributeRank", "words", "typo", "proximity", "sort", "wordPosition", "exactness"]`. These 3 hits correspond to documents for which `category` is equal to `physics`.

Thanks to the Meilisearch community for all the efforts that are being put into such an awesome tool!

Alessandro
author: acerioni

title: feat: implement streaming for document retrieval to avoid OOM crashes
body:
### Summary
This PR addresses #4383 by implementing a streaming response for both the GET /indexes/{index_uid}/documents and search routes (POST /search and GET /search).

Currently, Meilisearch deserializes and stores all requested documents/hits in RAM before sending them to the client. This results in Out Of Memory (OOM) crashes when high-concurrency search or retrieval requests fetch thousands of large documents.

### Changes
- **New Streaming Module**: Introduced streaming.rs which contains StreamedJsonObject and StreamedJsonArray wrappers to handle asynchronous JSON streaming using  utures and 	okio.
- **Refactored Document Retrieval**: Updated get_documents to first fetch DocumentIds and then stream the documents one-by-one from the database.
- **Refactored Search Pipeline**: 
    - Separated search metadata calculation from hit generation in perform_search.
    - Refactored make_hits to return an iterator instead of a Vec.
    - Introduced a streaming path in the search route handlers that sends metadata first, then streams hits as they are formatted.
- **Memory Efficiency**: Reduced memory footprint significantly for large document retrievals and high-limit search queries.

### Constraints
- **Personalization**: Reranking for personalization still requires all hits to be in memory, so the implementation gracefully falls back to non-streaming behavior when personalization is active.
- **Federated Search**: Similarly, federated search (multi-index) currently falls back to non-streaming as it requires merging and ranking across multiple sources.

I also analyzed vector search performance bottlenecks and commented on #6169 separately.

title: Are ACID all-or-nothing transactions supported by Meilisearch?
body:
Using Python. Sorry if this is a naive question. I see Meilisearch uses Tasks and WorkFlows, but there is no discussion of ACID in the documents, and the description of Tasks does not appear to conform to this use case. I thought all major databases supported some form of session-based multi-operation ACID transactions. 

Could someone speak to this? 
The individual transactions I want to fulfill are simple, but I presumed a formalized, batch-able model existed?

For instance, in my use case I have the following operations in a batch transaction.

```python
new_item = Item()
with client.session() as transaction:
  item = transaction.get(table_id, object_id)
  transaction.put(item, backup_table_id, object_id)
  transaction.put(new_item, table_id) 
```

If either of those .put() transactions fail I want the entirety of the operation undone: ACID.
I have also used ElasticSearch extensively in the past and I believe they even enable batchify of sessions.
So that I could define that transaction context window above, and call that itself with multiple items in batch.

The use case is simple enough that I can do this manually. Not a blocker.
But surprised and, once again, confused by the documentation at Meilisearch. </sad>
Really pulling this for a core value proposition. Thanks.

title: Cannot take snapshots on Windows due to map_size and page_size values
body:
**Describe the bug**
Index scheduler fails to initialize during snapshot creation on Windows, leading to an internal error and the inability to create snapshots. **To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Run Meilisearch on Windows (x86) with default options 2. Attempt to create snapshot 3. Snapshot fails with the following error: ``` Batch failed while doing: {"steps":[{"currentStep":"processing tasks","finished":0,"total":2},{"currentStep":"snapshot the index scheduler","finished":1,"total":6}],"percentage":8.333334} Batch failed map size (1310824018739) must be a multiple of the system page size (4096) ``` **Expected behavior**
The snapshot succeeds **Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem. **Meilisearch version:**
Reproduced on v1.27.0 and v1.29.0 **Additional context**
We have done analysis of the code where the error originates (found via trace logging) and we believe there is a missing call to `clamp_to_page_size` [here]() We see that the DEFAULT_BUDGET on Windows is 6TiB: ``` const DEFAULT_BUDGET: usize = 6 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024; // 6 TiB, 1 index ``` Naturally, this properly fits into the default page size of 4KiB (4096) for x86-64 machines: ``` 6597069766656÷4096 = 1610612736 ``` Given the following trace logs, we can further deduce what happens in the function to make things go awry: ``` memmap budget: 6597069766656B index budget: 3277060046848B 1 index of 1310824018739B can be opened simultaneously. ``` With the default `task_db_size` of 20GiB [here]() and a default `base_map_size` set to the max index size (2TiB) [here]() we can trace the calculations: ``` let mut budget = budget / 2; # 3298534883328 ... budget -= task_db_size; # 3277060046848 (value from trace log) ... let mut index_count = budget / base_map_size; # 1.490234375 < 2 -> enter the conditional ... let map_size = (budget * 2) / 5; # 1310824018739.2 floored to the value from the trace ``` This gets returned as the map_size and instantly fails when passed off to heed: `1310824018739 mod 4096 = 819` If we clamped the map_size to the page size before returning, we believe the issue would be fixed.

title: Introduce a delta-encoded bitmap
body:
This PR introduces a new method for reducing the database size. Our first measures showed that the size of the word-docids database was reduced by half (yes, 50%) and that the word-prefix-docids database was reduced by 30%.

### Changelog

We introduced a more efficient way to store internal data structures on disk. This new technique, called delta-encoding, is very space-efficient when storing many runs of increasing integers, which is the case for Meilisearch. Our measures showed that the database size can be reduced by up to 50% in some cases. Note that the engine will not convert your database to this new format immediately; instead, it will do so gradually during indexing, whenever a data structure is naturally modified. It's like the engine is gradually adopting the new format. This feature can be disabled by using the `--experimental-disable-delta-encoding` or by setting the environment variable `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_DELTA_ENCODING=true`.

## Notes for the reviewer(s)

Please check that I only converted `CboRoaringBitmapCodec` to `DeCboRoaringBitmapCodec`, as that is the only valid way to change the codec. `DeCboRoaringBitmapCodec` codecs can read `CboRoaringBitmapCodec` data but not `RoaringBitmapCodec` data, and this can cause many hard-to-debug errors if we don't check for it properly, since it will generate silent errors and bitmaps with invalid values (e.g., 1, 16, ...) will be generated when deserializing them.

This is why you should also double-check that the CLI/env var option is valid, and we must ensure that this new codec is not used in the cloud by default. I added a new workflow test to check that disabling delta-encoding works correctly. Note that disabling delta-encoding doesn't disable deserialization of delta-encoded bitmaps.

TBD: AVX (ARM64) is only. library bitpacking does support large buckets: determine if we want to disable encoding them on ARM.

## This PR makes forward-compatible changes

*Forward-compatible changes are changes to the database such that databases created in an older version of  Meilisearch are still valid in the new version of Meilisearch. They usually represent additive changes, like adding a new optional attribute or setting.*

### Detail the change to the DB format and why it is forward compatible

We introduced a new `DeCboRoaringBitmap` that is capable of deserializing the `CboRoaringBitmaps`, deserializing `DeRoaringBitmap`s (delta-encoded), and encoding the numbers as `DeRoaringBitmaps`. For this, we add a header to the serialization format and check the size of the serialized data; if it is below a threshold, it consists of raw u32s.
		
- [x] Forward-compatibility: A database created before this PR and using the features touched by this PR was able to be opened by a Meilisearch produced by the code of this PR.
- [x] Declarative test: add a [declarative test containing a dumpless upgrade](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/TESTING.md#typical-usage)
		A new declarative test named `disabled-delta-encoding` has been introduced and:
		  - Starts from v1.12 without the delta-encoding feature (as it didn't exist),
		  - Indexes some documents,
		  - Switches to the latest version of Meilisearch with delta-encoding **disabled**,
		  - Indexes more documents.
		Another declarative test named `enabled-delta-encoding` has been introduced and:
		  - Starts from v1.12 without the delta-encoding feature (as it didn't exist),
		  - Indexes some documents,
		  - Switches to the latest version of Meilisearch with delta-encoding **enabled**,
		  - Indexes more documents.

## To Do
- [x] Make sure the delta-encoding codec is named `DeRoaringBitmapCodec`.
- [x] Create a `DeCboRoaringBitmap` that manages all encodings.
- [x] Make sure we can disable the delta-encoding via an experimental CLI parameter.
- [ ] ~Implement the conditional compilation with an `fn()` instead of a boolean.~
	   Actually, branching always on the same branch is well optimized by CPUs. We can change this in a future version and [running a pass of PGO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Profile-guided_optimization) can drastically speed things up.
- [ ] Introduce an alias to simplify the usage in milli's index.
- [x] Add workflow tests to check that disabling delta-encoding works as expected:
	    Disable it after processing tasks, then continue processing more tasks.
- [x] Enable delta encoding by default. Make it possible to disable it by using the `MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_DELTA_ENCODING=true` env variable.

title: Inconsistent counts with Hybrid Search
body:
**Describe the bug**
An issue arises when using Hybrid search in combination with pagination.  Performing a search on page 1 using the following body:


```
{
    "filter": [
        "locale = nl"
    ],
    "rankingScoreThreshold": 0.7,
    "hybrid": {
        "embedder": "default",
        "semanticRatio": 0.7
    },
    "facets": [],
    "limit": 60,
    "page": 1,
    "hitsPerPage": 24,
    "showRankingScore": true,
    "showRankingScoreDetails": true,
    "q": "stripverhalen van suske en wiske"
}
```

Gives the following result:

``` {
    "hits": [...],
    "query": "stripverhalen van suske en wiske",
    "processingTimeMs": 1613,
    "hitsPerPage": 24,
    "page": 1,
    "totalPages": 7,
    "totalHits": 145,
    "facetDistribution": {},
    "facetStats": {},
    "semanticHitCount": 24
}
```

So we have 145 total hits.
When performing the same request for page 2 the results are like so:

```
{
    "hits": [...],
    "query": "stripverhalen van suske en wiske",
    "processingTimeMs": 1605,
    "hitsPerPage": 24,
    "page": 2,
    "totalPages": 6,
    "totalHits": 141,
    "facetDistribution": {},
    "facetStats": {},
    "semanticHitCount": 24
}
```


Here I get 141 total results. How can the total results differ between pages? Also the processingTimes are **very high.** I also saw strange things with facet counts being incorrect. Also the limit is not being applied. I understand using hybrid search it doesn't really "filter" out non-matching results, rather ranking it by semantical value. Though it doesn't seem very useful in many scenario's to return thousands of records when performing search queries on large indexes. 

**Expected behavior**
I would expect the counts to be correct and also the limit to be applied. There should be the possibility to put a cap on the amount of returned search results. I don't see a point in returning thousands of records (on large indexes) when using pagination. Not a living creature on this planet wil navigate to the 157th page to see the results. 

**Meilisearch version:**
v1.19.1

title: Feature request: Enable CI builds for ARMv7 (32-bit ARM) targets
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, Meilisearch does not provide CI builds for the `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` target (32-bit ARM architecture). Users wishing to deploy Meilisearch on older or embedded ARM platforms (such as Raspberry Pi 2/3 in 32-bit mode or similar SoCs) need prebuilt binaries or, at least, CI confirmation that the codebase builds and passes tests for this architecture. **Describe the solution you'd like**
Please add an `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` cross-compilation target to your GitHub Actions CI: * Add `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` to the build/test matrix. * Use either `cross` or Rust toolchain/native toolchain as appropriate to build the project for this architecture. * Optionally, provide published binaries or Docker images for ARMv7. **Describe alternatives you've considered** * Manual cross-compilation with Rust toolchain (installation and build tested locally, but no CI guarantee). * Using a multi-arch Docker build, but currently only `x86_64` and `aarch64` seem officially supported and tested. **Additional context** * [Rust platform support for Armv7]() * This would help users on 32-bit embedded hardware and expand Meilisearch's platform compatibility. Thank you for considering support for ARMv7 CI builds!

title: Configure batch size for embedder enabled index
body:
## Problem

I have multiple indexes, some of which have 1000's of (small) documents. The embedding template I use make these even smaller, however Meilisearch will always send 1 test request, then batches of 10. For OpenAI on Azure, this very quickly results in 429's - and an index loading becomes an excruciatingly long process. The actual limit on tokens per minute is _well_ below the quota though - indicating I can batch many more documents per request.

## Proposed solution

When configuring an index with an [embedder](https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/settings#embedders-object), it would be great to configure either an explicit batch size or some factor of 'characters-per-token' that Meilisearch could use to perform dynamic batching.

As it stands now, v1.18.0 - Meilisearch will send batches of 10. 

To make it more better, if this could be described in a 'characters-per-token' factor along with 'tokens-per-batch'; when set, each batch is built up by accumulating the estimated tokens given those two values before sending off a batch of documents for embedding.

---

One 'hack' I tried was to add a proxy that batched these requests into larger requests - but quickly realized (unsurprisingly in hindsight) that these requests are done sequentially.

Happy to try taking a stab at implementing this. :)

title: Meilisearch document/fetch returns no hits when using a sort that has identical value to previous document when the offset is directly on that position.
body:
Hello everyone,
We’ve recently encountered this bug. In the report below, I’ll explain the exact issue we observed and how to reproduce it.

I would be greatly pleased if this could be look at for a later release of Meilisearch. until then, thanks in advance for reading this bug report 😄 

# **Describe the bug**
As the title states, when using the **`/documents/fetch`** endpoint to fetch a large number of documents from the Meilisearch index, we’ve encountered an issue. If you use the **`sort`** with the **`offset`** parameter and multiple records share the same value in the sorted field, Meilisearch fails to fetch the second instance of that record when the offset is set precisely at that point.

# **To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a new index
2. Fill index with a set of data that includes a field for example use created_at with a ISO timestamp
3. Have multiple documents that have the same created_at iso timestamp 
4. filter using the endpoint **`/documents/fetch`** with the following body:
```
{
	"limit": 1,
	"offset": ,
	"sort": ["created_at:asc"]
}
// make sure that the offset is the point of the second instance, 
// of a document with the same created_at iso timestamp
```

5. you will return 0 hits. no matter how large the limit is.

# **Expected behavior**
What we expect to happen is the following:
When we apply the filters as described above, the result for that offset should be returned correctly, rather than showing 0 hits.

In other words, even when multiple documents share the same value in the sorted field, Meilisearch should continue returning consistent results across paginated requests. Each document should remain retrievable regardless of its position relative to other documents with identical sort values.

# **Screenshots**
Due to the privacy of the data, i can't show screenshot so ill be using example body's to show our results:
### Path that results in no hits:
Request body:
```
request body:
{
	"limit": 1,
	"offset": 400,
	"sort": ["created_at:asc"]
}
response body: 
{
    "results": [],
    "offset": 400,
    "limit": 1,
    "total": 12345
}
```
### Path that results in getting actual data including offset 400:
```
request body:
{
	"limit": 3,
	"offset": 399,
	"sort": ["created_at:asc"]
}
response body: 
{
    "results": [
        {
            "id": "399",
            "created_at": 1761292222,
            "updated_at": 1761292248,
            "book_name": "Lorum Ipsum 1"
        },
        {
            "id": "400",
            "created_at": 1761292222,
            "updated_at": 1761292249,
            "book_name": "Lorum Ipsum 2"
        },
        {
            "id": "401",
            "created_at": 1761292229,
            "updated_at": 1761292252,
            "book_name": "Lorum Ipsum 3"
        }
    ],
    "offset": 400,
    "limit": 1,
    "total": 12345
}
```

# **Meilisearch version:**
all version from 1.19.1 to 1.24.0 (LTS at time of writing this bug report)

# **Additional context**
When we first encountered this issue, we tested a lot of different things to try and determine why it was happening on our side.

Things we noticed:

1. When updating the created_at value of the second document to be just 1 tick later, the document was fetched correctly.
2. This issue occurred across multiple instances, versions, and indexes.

# **Workaround for this issue (until it is fixed)**
The workaround we found for this issue is as follows:
We now, by default, add the `id:asc` field to our filter requests. This ensures that if Meilisearch cannot sort solely on created_at, it will also sort by id, returning the correct document at the desired offset.

title: Chat route improvement and follow up
body:
This is a tracking issue to follow up on [the chat completions route](). We released the chat route in [#5556](). I'll list the different concerns and fixes to introduce to strengthen the usage of the feature: - [ ] Store chat workspace settings in the dumps - [ ] Make sure we can rollback to pre-PR (chat settings in index settings) ### Support more LLM-providers - [ ] Reintroduce the support of Gemini. - [ ] Support Qwen3 - [ ] Support DeepSeek - [ ] Support a generic interface ### Improve the documentation Some users do not understand some parts of the documentation ([private link]()). ### Add more analytics We should add enough analytics to tell who's using our feature and how often. - [ ] Count the tokens and expose them in the stats (or somewhere else). - [ ] Add analytics when changing the `/chats` workspace settings. - [X] [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5709]() ### Improve the chat completions parameters By accepting any JSON object as input and only requiring the `model`, `messages`, `stream`, and `tools` fields, we can support any chat completions API as long as they have compatible outputs. - [ ] Document the compatible APIs. - [ ] (idea) [Accept any field]() as input and only care about the interesting ones. - [ ] Explain the input and output (mirror the underlying LLM). - [ ] Make the tool calls compatible with the `source` setting (OpenAI, Mistral, Ollama, or Anthropic) - [X] Allow incremental changes of the chat hybrid search settings [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2137368486](). - [ ] List a subset of allowed models to be used. ### Improve the non-streamed chat completions route The chat completions route is very good, but only the streamed version. We must work on the non-streamed version to improve it. - [ ] Ensure correct tool support. - [ ] Ensure correct error report. - [ ] Enable the route again. ### Improve the index choice speed When the LLM receives a question, it uses the index uids and descriptions to decide which index to query. Unfortunately, the index description is stored in the indexes directly, necessitating opening them to fetch the description and maybe not even querying them afterward. Opening indexing can be slow, especially when they are not already open. - [ ] Store the index descriptions in the index scheduler (for speed). - [X] Introduce the `IndexScheduler::try_for_each_index` method capable of filtering on the index name before deciding to open it [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2137906663]() ### Improve the way we are doing the internal search Currently, we use a bunch of internal mixtures to perform the searches and retrieve the top k documents. However, we should simplify this part by directly calling our search route. This would simplify the code and give us more features and information. - [ ] Directly call the actual search route using the [actix-web `url_for` method](). - [ ] Change the agent when calling the search route. - [ ] Return all search info (estimated total hits, hits, scores) from the sources. - [X] (idea) Expose and use the ranking score as a measure of confidence for the LLM [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2138080413]() ### Improve the index chat setting We introduced a new `chat` subsetting in the index settings, allowing users to define index-related settings, prompts, and search settings. - [ ] Rename the `prompts` parameter? ### Improve the chat completions support in keys We shipped basic support for chat completions in the keys. Unfortunately, for security reasons, we need to support more features. - [ ] (optional) Make chat workspace settings capable of restricting accessible indexes.
Personally, I prefer the API keys to restrict the accessible indexes. - [X] Restrict the API Key to specific chat workspaces [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2137906663]() ### Code improvements - [X] Remove the manual implementation of Deserr on some types? [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2137308770]() - [ ] Factorize more code - [ ] Use the `async-openai`'s `byot` feature to support more LLM providers [https://github.com/64bit/async-openai/pull/368#issuecomment-2952916801]() - [ ] Create new config types for the different LLM providers [https://github.com/64bit/async-openai/pull/369#issuecomment-2952914668]() - [X] Move the Function support in the utils file [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2137885161]() - [X] Create a struct wrapper to simplify the global function calling struct [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2138107112]() - [X] Add more comments to explain better stuff [https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/5556#discussion_r2138145271]()

body:
Meilisearch returns invalid facet counts in the facet distribution. When a filter is added to a query some of the facet counts increase. This issue is directly related to [this Cloud issue (internal link)](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch-support/issues/178#issuecomment-2110265647) and you can find the datasets and settings there.

**To Reproduce**
1. Send a simple query: `{"q":"glam","filter":[],"facets":["tags"],"page":0}`
2. Look at the facet counts: `{"backpack": 9, "bag": 15}`
3. Send the same query with a filter: `{"q":"glam","filter":[["tags = \"backpack\""]],"facets":["tags"],"page":0}`
4. Look at the facet counts **increase**: `{"backpack": 43, "backpacking": 1, "bag": 43}`
5. Send the another query with another filter: `{"q":"glam","filter":[["tags = \"backpack\"", "tags = \"bag\""]],"facets":["tags"],"page":0}`
6. Look at the facet counts **increase** again: `{"backpack": 43, "backpacking": 1, "bag": 67}`

**Expected behavior**
The facet count must be more precise/stable and must even decrease if you constrain the query more with filters. By using `page: 0` or a very high `limit`, the engine must be exhaustive on the facet counts.

**Meilisearch version:**
v1.8.0

**Additional context**
On the Cloud, but probably not related.

author: ronnyholm

title: OS error 5 when adding lots of prefixable unique words to an index
body:
**Describe the bug**
When indexing documents that contain a lot of long words (e.g. `1660534213676785670`), the FST that contains the words and that is used by Meilisearch to compute prefix grows a lot. This FST is stored as a single value inside of a LMDB table.

LMDB values are limited in theory to about 2^32 bytes, but in practice depending on the OS it could be less than 2^31 bytes (see these issues for [Linux](https://bugs.openldap.org/show_bug.cgi?id=10054) and [macOS](https://bugs.openldap.org/show_bug.cgi?id=9736)), so the unbounded FST growth can result in `EIO` being returned by LMDB as the value reaches the maximum size permitted in practice.

This issue is one of the issues encountered in https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/3654.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Set the maximum number of opened files to a huge number: `ulimit -Sn 10000`
2. Write the following script to `gen_docs_bigid.py`:
```py
import random
random.seed(42)

big_id = 1_660_534_213_676_785_670
big_value = 1_000_000_000_000_785_670
big_random = 10_000_000_000_000_785_670

for i in range(0,100_000_000):
	print(f'{{ "id": "{big_id + i + random.randint(big_random, big_random + big_id)}", "value" : "{big_value + random.randint(big_random, big_random + big_id) + i}" }}')
```
3. Run the script: `python3 gen_docs_bigid.py > big_docs.njson`
4. Start Meilisearch with a HTTP payload size of 10G: `meilisearch --http-payload-size-limit 10GB`
5. Add the document to an index: 
```
curl \
  -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/big_fst/documents' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' \
  -T big_docs.njson
```
6. Wait for the indexing to process
7. When the task is no longer processing, check in the tasks that it failed with OS error 5

The FST that Meilisearch failed to write to LMDB contains about 200M entries at this point.

**Expected behavior**
Indexing succeeds without errors

**Meilisearch version:**
v1.1.1, but not new in this version

title: Major lack of documentation in codebase
body:
**Describe the bug**
The codebase significantly lacks documentation. As a newly introduced developer, it makes it hard for me to navigate the codebase and quickly identify which item does what. The documentation is needed as a source of intuition for evaluating whether some code item is valuable for the end-user, and whether it should be modified, and how exactly it should be modified to accomplish the desired behavior. 

Without the said documentation, the codebase can easily become a jungle of functions/structs/enums/traits whose names only suffice for achieving a ballpark of correct understanding rather than the exact understanding required to modify the correct code in the correct way. 

Documenting the codebase may constitute a significant upfront investment, but I believe it will pay off in the long run. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
`cargo doc --open --document-private-items` 
Alternatively, just look in the code on any arbitrary function/struct/impl/trait/etc. This problem seems to be pervasive throughout most of the codebase. 

**Expected behavior**
Each code item (struct, impl, trait, enum, function) should have documentation that explains how the given code item relates to the greater context from the end-user's point of view.

title: Fix error when setting a wrong key in the config file
body:

```bash
Error: unknown field `no_analytic` at line 1 column 1
```

author: curquiza

title: Dockerfile: don't use `root` as default user
body:
Our Dockerfile to build the MeiliSearch's image uses the `root` user. We are aware this is not a good practice. However, we encountered many issues when trying to change this.

History:
- This PR https://github.com/meilisearch/MeiliSearch/pull/1759 (using the `meili` user instead of `root`) was accepted, merged, and released in v0.24.0
- We figured out this led to many issues detailed [here](https://github.com/meilisearch/MeiliSearch/issues/1969): one in the documentation (easily fixed) and one regarding Linux users.
- We tried to fix the Linux issue, without any success
- We reverted the PR and released this in v0.25.0 https://github.com/meilisearch/MeiliSearch/pull/2032

Before implementing this issue, we mean, use a non-root user for our Dockerfile, please ensure you took a look a the [whole issue conversation](https://github.com/meilisearch/MeiliSearch/issues/1969) since many things have been tried.
author: curquiza

title: Improve the geosearch
body:
Multiple things can / should be done to improve the geosearch:
- Currently, we need to `Deserialize` the whole `RTree` in memory before being able to do anything. This consumes a lot of RAM and thus is quite slow.
    => We should patch [rstar](https://github.com/georust/rstar) to add the possibility to parse the `RTree` part by part
- When creating an `RTree` for [the first time](https://github.com/meilisearch/milli/blob/geosearch/milli/src/update/index_documents/typed_chunk.rs#L184) we should use the function [bulk_load](https://docs.rs/rstar/0.9.1/rstar/struct.RTree.html#method.bulk_load)
- Add the possibility to sort the position by descending order. It will also require to modify rstar
